items.title: Embedding LLMs in the patient portal to summarize acute minor illness information: a three-arm experimental study.
items.body: BACKGROUND: Patient portals provide direct access to clinical encounter data; however, comprehension barriers, especially for patients with limited health literacy, frequently prevent meaningful use, even for common acute conditions. Large language models (LLMs) embedded in the portal interface may convert clinical documentation into accessible plain-language summaries, yet no experimental study has evaluated this approach for acute minor illness. OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the impact of embedding two commercially available frontier LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4.5 [Anthropic] and GPT-5.1 Thinking [OpenAI]) into the patient portal of a small primary care clinic on patients' comprehension of information about acute minor illnesses, portal engagement, self-management adherence, and unnecessary healthcare utilization. METHODS: We conducted a three-arm experimental study at a five-physician primary care practice. Adults (≥18 years) presenting with acute upper respiratory infection, influenza-like illness, or similar acute minor ailment were assigned 1:1:1 to: (A) Claude Sonnet 4.5 portal summaries, (B) GPT-5.1 Thinking portal summaries, or (C) standard portal access (control). The primary outcome was health information comprehension at Day 14, assessed via a study-specific, pilot-tested 10-item quiz (0-100 scale). A clinician audit of 20% of LLM summaries assessed accuracy and safety. RESULTS: Of 186 enrolled participants, 174 completed the 4-week follow-up (93.5% retention). At Day 14, comprehension scores were significantly higher in LLM arms versus control (Claude: M = 81.4, SD = 9.3; GPT-5.1: M = 79.6, SD = 10.1; control: M = 63.2, SD = 12.8; F(2,169) = 47.34, p < 0.001, partial η = 0.36). Both LLM arms showed significantly higher total portal login frequency (Claude: p = 0.001; GPT: p = 0.007), longer session durations, and greater self-management adherence (p = 0.007) compared with the control. Unnecessary return visits were approximately 61% lower in combined LLM arms (OR = 0.34, 95% CI [0.14-0.81], p = 0.015). Minor factual imprecision rates in audited summaries were 5.7% (Claude) and 11.8% (GPT-5.1), with zero clinically significant hallucinations across all audited summaries. No significant difference was observed between the two LLMs. CONCLUSION: LLM-embedded patient portal summaries significantly improved comprehension of acute minor illnesses and reduced unnecessary healthcare utilization in a primary care setting. Because the intervention combined an LLM-generated plain-language summary with its prominent presentation in a dedicated portal panel, the observed effects should be interpreted as the result of this combined plain-language-plus-interface intervention rather than as a test of LLM capability alone. Both models performed comparably and safely, supporting the feasibility of further evaluation in diverse clinical settings. Further multi-site replication and implementation science studies are needed.
items.why: This three-arm experimental study embedded two frontier large language models (LLMs) into a primary care patient portal to generate plain-language summaries of acute illness information, finding significantly higher comprehension scores, portal engagement, and self-management adherence versus standard portal access, plus a 61% lower odds of unnecessary return visits (odds ratio 0.34). This is a rare randomized comparison with a hard utilization endpoint and clinician-audited safety data, making it one of the more substantive patient-facing LLM evaluations this cycle.
items.plain: Researchers randomly assigned patients to get AI-written summaries of their visit information (from two different chatbot models) or the usual portal text, and found the AI summaries led to much better understanding of their illness, more use of the patient portal, and 61% fewer unnecessary follow-up visits. This is notable because it is a real controlled experiment with an outcome that matters, not just a rating of how good the chatbot's answers sounded.

items.title: Deep Time-to-Event Models for Intrapartum Fetal Monitoring.
items.body: Timely detection of fetal distress during labor is a central pursuit of modern obstetric care. The primary measure used in this regard is fetal heart rate and contraction monitoring (echocardiotocography or CTG), which provides a continuous signal during labor. The vast majority of machine learning applications to CTG assume access to a 30 to 60 minute window just prior to delivery, which makes an untenable assumption that the timing of delivery is known. In this work, we reframe the problem as a time-to-event prediction task. We develop deep time-to-event models to predict the joint probability of imminent delivery and fetal acidosis, a biomarker of fetal hypoxia collected from umbilical cord gas after delivery. We develop a framework for this problem, drawing on deep discrete-time survival methods and marked point processes, adapting each to this particular setting (i.e., continuous physiological signals, fully observed events, partially observed labels). One approach dubbed Marked DeepHit accurately estimates delivery within one hour at multiple elapsed-time landmarks, with test-set AUROC of 0.837 [95% CI 0.692-0.970] and 0.935 [0.858-0.964] at 6 and 12 hours into labor, respectively. We find that these models also achieve competitive performance near delivery time compared to prior models trained specifically on the end of tracing, and outperform other clinical feature-based proposals, both on internal and external validation at a second site. These results give a proof-of-principle to support future prospective deployment of AI-EFM during labor.
items.why: This study reframes intrapartum fetal heart rate monitoring (cardiotocography, CTG) as a time-to-event prediction problem rather than assuming a fixed pre-delivery window, developing a deep learning model called Marked DeepHit that jointly predicts imminent delivery and fetal acidosis, achieving test-set area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.837 to 0.935 at 6 and 12 hours into labor, with validation at a second external site. The external validation and the novel time-to-event framing that avoids the unrealistic assumption of known delivery timing make this a methodologically meaningful advance toward real-world deployable intrapartum monitoring, though it remains a proof-of-principle rather than a deployed clinical tool.
items.plain: Researchers built an AI model that continuously watches a baby's heart rate during labor and predicts, at any point in time, how likely the baby is to be delivered soon and whether it might be in distress, without needing to know in advance when delivery will happen. The model was tested at a second hospital different from where it was built, which is an important sign that it might work well in real-world settings beyond where it was trained.

items.title: CTG-FRAME: development and validation of a multi‑modal deep learning for intrapartum escalation support and severe fetal acidemia prediction.
items.body: BACKGROUND: Cardiotocography is important for continuous intrapartum fetal surveillance, yet its clinical effectiveness is limited by high inter-observer variability and a false-positive burden of approximately 60%. These limitations contribute to unnecessary intervention while delaying recognition of fetal acidemia. For clinical use, decision-support systems must not only achieve high accuracy but also define their role in guiding escalation of care. METHODS: We developed and evaluated CTG-FRAME (CardioTocoGraphy-Fetal Risk Assessment and Monitoring Engine), an end-to-end deep learning decision-support framework for identifying risk of severe fetal acidemia (umbilical arterial pH < 7.05) using fetal heart rate and uterine contraction signals. The framework integrates self-supervised momentum-contrast pre-training, a hybrid ResNet-temporal convolutional encoder, bidirectional cross-attention, and a Transformer to capture global temporal context. The model was trained and internally validated on the CTU-UHB dataset (n = 552; ~8% acidemia) using three-fold cross-validation. External transferability and calibration were assessed in a separate multicentre cohort (SPaM; n = 300; ~20% acidemia) not used during model development. CTG-FRAME outputs a probability of acidemia, estimates continuous pH severity, and identifies signal segments contributing to each prediction. Training employed a difficulty-aware multi-stage curriculum to address severe class imbalance. Model performance was evaluated using AUROC, sensitivity, specificity, and agreement measures. RESULTS: On CTU-UHB, the model achieved an AUROC of 0.888, with sensitivity 0.850 and specificity 0.964 at the predefined operating threshold (≈0.52). External evaluation of SPaM showed predicted abnormality rates consistent with cohort prevalence without re-tuning, indicating calibration preservation across sites. Ablation analysis demonstrated that the staged curriculum was necessary to prevent collapse to majority-class prediction, and that the self-supervised pre-training substantially improved pH estimation accuracy. CONCLUSIONS: CTG-FRAME is designed to facilitate the escalation of clinical review rather than autonomous clinical action by defining a clear decision-analytic operating region and generating interpretable, context-linked evidence. This work advances obstetric artificial intelligence by making clinical intent, operating trade-offs, and workflow roles explicit, moving beyond accuracy toward verifiable bedside utility.
items.why: CTG-FRAME is a multi-module deep learning framework for predicting severe fetal acidemia from cardiotocography (CTG) signals, trained and cross-validated on the CTU-UHB dataset (n=552) and externally tested on a separate multicenter cohort (SPaM, n=300), achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.888 with sensitivity 0.85 and specificity 0.964, and showing preserved calibration without retuning on external data. This is a genuine external validation of an intrapartum decision-support tool addressing a well-known clinical problem, high false-positive burden in fetal monitoring, making it one of the stronger obstetric AI entries this week, though the acidemia prevalence differs notably between cohorts.
items.plain: Researchers built an AI system that reads fetal heart rate and contraction patterns during labor to flag babies at risk of dangerously low blood oxygen, and tested it on a different hospital's patients than the ones it was trained on, correctly identifying 85 percent of true cases. This matters because current fetal monitoring causes a lot of false alarms, and testing on an outside hospital's data is a meaningful check that the tool might generalize, though the two patient groups had different rates of the condition.

items.title: Feasibility and Reproducibility of a Structure-Guided Deep Learning Model for Automatic Detection of the Standard Sagittal Plane in First-Trimester Nuchal Translucency Assessment Using 3D Ultrasound.
items.body: OBJECTIVES: Accurate nuchal translucency (NT) measurement for assessing the risk of fetal genetic abnormalities requires precise acquisition of the mid-sagittal plane (MSP). However, achieving an appropriate MSP is technically challenging due to anatomical variability and operator dependence inherent in conventional 2-dimensional (2D) ultrasound. This study aimed to develop and validate a novel deep learning algorithm for automated fetal MSP extraction from 3-dimensional (3D) ultrasound volumes utilizing intracranial structure segmentation to overcome the limitations of conventional methods reliant on facial landmarks. METHODS: In this prospective study, we developed and evaluated "3D MSP-net," a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based model for automated MSP extraction, involving singleton pregnant women undergoing first-trimester NT screening. Using achieved 3D volume data, 3D MSP-net was validated against the conventional 2D manual method and a commercially available rule-based automated system (5D NT™). Two maternal-fetal medicine (MFM) specialists independently assessed the resulting MPSs to determine the performance for demonstrating the feasibility and high reproducibility of the 3D MSP-net. RESULTS: 3D MSP-net achieved an MSP extraction success rate of 91.6%, comparable to that of the conventional 2D manual method and significantly superior to the rule-based 3D algorithm. NT measurements were comparable between the conventional 2D manual approach and MSPs derived from 3D MSP-net (1.4 ± 0.5 mm versus 1.4 ± 0.4 mm; p = .444). These results were reproducible on external validation. Moreover, the 3D MSP-net maintained robust performance even under challenging conditions, such as increased maternal body mass index and different scan deviation angles. CONCLUSION: The 3D MSP-net, our artificial intelligence (AI) model that utilizes intracranial landmarks for MSP reconstruction, enables improved efficiency, standardization, and reliability for first-trimester fetal screening addressing a key challenge in prenatal diagnostics.
items.why: This prospective study developed 3D MSP-net, a convolutional neural network (CNN) that automatically extracts the mid-sagittal plane (MSP) from 3D ultrasound for first-trimester nuchal translucency (NT) measurement, achieving a 91.6% success rate comparable to manual methods and superior to a commercial rule-based system, with nuchal translucency measurements statistically equivalent to manual assessment and reproducible on external validation. The robustness across maternal body mass index and scan angles plus genuine external validation make this a credible step toward reducing operator dependence in a widely performed screening test.
items.plain: Researchers built an AI tool that automatically finds the correct image angle needed to measure a fold of skin on the back of a fetus's neck, used in first-trimester screening for genetic conditions. The tool matched expert manual measurements and beat an existing automated competitor, and it kept working well even in harder cases like heavier patients, which is a meaningful improvement for standardizing this common prenatal test.

items.title: Evaluating the impact of social determinants of health on model performance and fairness in artificial intelligence for glaucoma progression prediction.
items.body: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of incorporating community-level social determinants of health (SDoH) on the performance and algorithmic fairness of artificial intelligence (AI) models trained to predict glaucoma progression to surgery. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This multicenter study included 63 268 glaucoma patients across 12 centers. Using electronic health records and community-level SDoH features (Distressed Communities Index [DCI] and rural-urban commuting area [RUCA] codes), we developed XGBoost models to predict progression to incisional glaucoma surgery. We compared SDoH-unaware and SDoH-aware models across an internal test set and 3 diverse external test sets, evaluating area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) (performance) and generalized equalized odds (GEO) (fairness). RESULTS: Including SDoH features resulted in negligible changes in predictive performance across the internal and all external test sets. However, the SDoH-aware model improved algorithmic fairness (achieving lower GEO scores) in the internal set (0.098 vs 0.216) and a mixed-population external site (0.172 vs 0.378). Conversely, inclusion of SDoH marginally improved at a highly urbanized, low-DCI external site (0.491 vs 0.504) and failed to improve at a rural, high-DCI external site (0.241 vs 0.228). DISCUSSION: Incorporating SDoH features can improve algorithmic fairness regarding socioeconomic disparities without sacrificing predictive accuracy; however, these benefits do not universally transfer to external sites with demographically dissimilar cohorts. CONCLUSION: Incorporating community-level SDoH features into glaucoma prediction models improved algorithmic fairness with respect to socioeconomic disparities, without significantly altering predictive accuracy. However, fairness benefits did not universally generalize to demographically dissimilar external cohorts. AI models require rigorous external validation across diverse populations to ensure equity prior to clinical implementation.
items.why: This multicenter study of 63,268 glaucoma patients across 12 centers tested whether adding community-level social determinants of health (SDoH, such as area deprivation and rural-urban location) to an XGBoost model predicting progression to glaucoma surgery improved algorithmic fairness, finding reduced generalized equalized odds (GEO, a fairness metric comparing error rates across subgroups) at the internal site and one external site but not at two demographically different external sites. The large multicenter design with external validation is a methodological strength, and the finding that fairness gains do not transfer across sites is directly relevant to anyone deploying prediction models across health systems.
items.plain: Researchers tested whether adding neighborhood-level information, like local poverty levels and whether an area is rural or urban, to an AI model predicting who needs glaucoma surgery would make the model treat different patient groups more fairly. Across more than 63,000 patients at 12 medical centers, the extra information helped fairness at some locations but not others, showing that a fix that works in one hospital system may not work in another.

items.title: MADE: leveraging informative missingness and temporal evaluation for electronic health record-based deterioration prediction in general wards.
items.body: OBJECTIVE: Electronic health record (EHR) time series are irregularly sampled and frequently incomplete, with missingness potentially carrying clinically informative signals. We developed Masked-Attention-based timestamp-wise Data Embedding (MADE), a missingness-aware model for continuous prediction of deterioration in general wards, and evaluated it across heterogeneous hospitals. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Observed variables were tokenized into feature-specific embeddings and processed by a masked-attention Transformer, followed by bi-LSTM temporal aggregation for risk prediction. MADE was evaluated for major adverse event (MAE) and sepsis in 1 internal (SVH) and 2 external cohorts (AMC, HUMC) against conventional and deep learning baselines. Ablation studies compared no imputation with last observation carried forward (LOCF) and multiple imputations by chained equations (MICE). Discriminative performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and precision-recall curve (AUPRC). Clinical utility and reliability were assessed using decision curve analysis, Brier score, and expected calibration error (ECE). RESULTS: MADE achieved strong discrimination for MAE (AUROC 0.966/0.902/0.825 for SVH/AMC/HUMC) and sepsis (AUROC 0.934/0.874/0.776). The no-imputation configuration generally outperformed LOCF and MICE, particularly for MAE and for sepsis AUPRC, supporting preservation of informative missingness. Decision curves showed favorable net benefit for MAE and competitive benefit for sepsis. Calibration indicated modest underestimation at higher risks, suggesting site-specific recalibration. DISCUSSION: MADE mitigates limitations of fixed grid and imputation-dependent EHR modeling by jointly leveraging observed values and missingness patterns under heterogeneous sampling. CONCLUSION: MADE supports scalable observation-aligned risk monitoring, particularly for MAE, while sepsis prediction may require site-specific recalibration or feature-set adaptation under cross-institution domain shifts.
items.why: This study developed Masked-Attention-based timestamp-wise Data Embedding (MADE), a missingness-aware transformer model for predicting deterioration in general hospital wards, validated across one internal and two external cohorts, achieving area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.966/0.902/0.825 for major adverse events and 0.934/0.874/0.776 for sepsis, with the no-imputation configuration outperforming standard imputation methods. The multi-site external validation and the finding that missingness itself carries predictive signal are methodologically notable, though calibration degraded at higher risk levels, suggesting site-specific recalibration is needed before deployment.
items.plain: Researchers built an AI model that predicts when hospital patients on general wards are about to get seriously worse, using the pattern of which measurements are missing as a clue rather than just filling in the gaps. Tested at three different hospitals, the model worked quite well, especially for catching major health crises, but its confidence in high-risk predictions wasn't perfectly matched to reality, meaning it would need fine-tuning before being trusted in each new hospital.

items.title: The Building and Application of a Machine Learning Model on Predicting Euploid Blastocysts in IVF Treatments Without PGT-A.
items.body: Embryologists could not know whether blastocysts were euploid or not in in-vitro fertilization treatments without preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy. However, preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy technology which might impair the developmental potency of blastocysts was in strict limitation in China. Therefore, a non-invasive method was necessary for embryologists to select euploid embryos as far as possible. A machine learning model based on preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy results, development dynamics, morphology of blastocysts and female age was built by two-logistic regression analysis. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of the model was 0.877. The accuracy rate, precision rate, recall rate, f-score, true negative rate, false positive rate, false negative rate of the model when performed in independent data set were 77.35%, 77.49%, 72.55%, 74.94%, 81.55%, 18.45%, 27.45%, respectively. Besides, the false positive rate of the model on predicting euploid blastocysts was significantly lower than Gardner grade and KIDScore D5. When selected blastocysts by the model, the frozen embryo transfer outcomes improved significantly than the frozen embryo transfer outcomes which selected blastocysts by Gardner selection. The predictive model had potency in selecting euploid blastocysts in in-vitro fertilization treatments without preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy technology.
items.why: This study built a logistic regression-based machine learning model using preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) results, morphokinetic development, morphology, and maternal age to predict blastocyst euploidy, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.877 on an independent validation set and a lower false positive rate than Gardner grading or KIDScore D5; frozen embryo transfer outcomes improved when embryos were selected by the model versus conventional morphology grading. The comparison against established clinical grading systems and the reported improvement in a real treatment outcome make this more actionable than typical embryo-selection models, though details on study design and cohort size are sparse.
items.plain: Scientists built an AI tool that predicts whether an embryo has the normal number of chromosomes without needing an invasive genetic test, using things like how the embryo develops, its shape, and the mother's age. When doctors used this tool to pick embryos for transfer, pregnancy outcomes were better than when they used standard visual grading alone, which is a meaningful real-world result.

items.title: Foundation model-powered deep learning of endometrial histology for predicting the cumulative live birth of an in vitro fertilization cycle.
items.body: Objective and reproducible assessment of endometrial receptivity is essential for optimizing in vitro fertilization (IVF) success, yet traditional histological dating suffers from observer variability. This study investigated whether deep learning of hematoxylin and eosin histology images could support cumulative live birth prediction in IVF. An end-to-end ResNet-18 was compared with a UNI2-h-based pipeline, using UNI2-h as a frozen feature extractor. Ten-fold cross-validation ensembles were developed from natural-cycle endometrial biopsies and evaluated in an internal held-out cohort with live birth outcomes. Additional phase-based evaluation was performed, which tested the performance in distinguishing LH + 7 versus non-LH + 7 phases. A luminal epithelium (LE)-focused design was also assessed to examine whether concentrating on maternal-embryo interface could improve fertility-oriented learning. The whole-slide ResNet-18 model performed well in internal outcome-based testing but near random in external phase-based testing. In contrast, the UNI2-h model with mean pooling and a multilayer perceptron classifier showed less divergent performance, with ensembled AUROCs of 0.74 ± 0.03 in internal outcome-based evaluation, and 0.90 ± 0.05 in external phase-based testing. Despite a smaller training set, LE-focused models retained comparable performance. In internal outcome-based testing, LE-focused ResNet-18 and UNI2-h models achieved AUROCs of 0.71 ± 0.03 and 0.74 ± 0.09 respectively. External phase-based testing yielded AUROCs of 0.80 ± 0.16 for ResNet-18, and 0.84 ± 0.06 for UNI2-h. Grad-CAM review of LE-focused ResNet-18 models showed attention commonly on LE-alone or mixed with adjacent stroma. In multimodal analyses, integrated models incorporating histology significantly outperformed the clinical metadata-only model. Integrated model's feature weighting showed dominant histology outputs, smaller contributions from estradiol and maternal age, and negligible contributions from progesterone, endometrial thickness, and BMI. These findings support histology-based AI for fertility-oriented endometrial assessment and highlight biologically informed design and repurposed foundation models as promising bases for clinically meaningful prediction.
items.why: This study compared an end-to-end convolutional network against a frozen foundation model feature extractor (UNI2-h) for predicting cumulative live birth from endometrial histology images in in vitro fertilization (IVF) patients, finding the foundation model approach generalized better to an external phase-based test cohort (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUROC, of 0.90 versus near-random for the standard model) despite lower performance on the internal outcome-based task. The divergence between internal and external performance highlights a genuine generalization problem relevant to anyone building histology-based prediction tools, and the finding that pretrained foundation models transfer better is a useful methodological signal even though absolute performance (AUROC 0.74 internally) remains modest for clinical use.
items.plain: Researchers tested two types of AI that look at microscope images of the womb lining to predict whether an IVF cycle will lead to a live birth, comparing a standard image-reading AI to one built on a large pretrained AI model. The pretrained model held up much better when tested on new data from a different context, while the standard model performed barely better than guessing, showing that some AI designs generalize better than others even if neither is yet accurate enough for routine clinical use.

items.title: A hybrid deep learning framework for automated treatment planning in cervical cancer radiotherapy.
items.body: BACKGROUND: Radiation therapy treatment planning is a time-consuming trial-and-error process, and the plan quality is heavily dependent on planners' experiences, resulting in a strong demand for automated planning methods that can rapidly generate uniformly high-quality plans. PURPOSE: This study aimed to develop a hybrid automated deep learning-based plan optimization (HALO) framework, integrating deep learning fluence prediction and optimization, multileaf collimator (MLC) sequencing, and GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo dose computation. HALO was designed to ensure robust plan generation for cervical cancer intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT). METHODS: The proposed HALO framework incorporated several functional modules. First, a dose-guided Fluence Prediction Network (DG-FPN) was developed. A total of 120 cervical cancer clinical IMRT plans were collected to train the DG-FPN, of which 90 plans were assigned for training, 10 for validation, and 20 for testing. The neural network took patients' computed tomography (CT) anatomy as input and predicted the 3D dose distribution and fluence maps. Next, the predicted fluence maps were further optimized to meet dose-volume constraints (DVCs), and then the refined fluence maps were converted into deliverable segments using an MLC sequencing algorithm. Finally, dose calculation was performed using a GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo engine. The 20 patients in the testing set were used to evaluate the HALO method, and the plan deliverability was validated by patient-specific IMRT Quality Assurance (QA). RESULTS: The DG-FPN achieved superior fluence prediction accuracy compared to previous work, with a median mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.055 and a structural similarity index (SSIM) of 0.94. The automated framework generated high-quality plans and reduced dose to adjacent OARs, with Vdecreased from 46.5 ± 5.0% to 41.5 ± 4.8% (p = 0.008)for bladder, Vdecreased from 31.5 ± 8.2% to 29.2 ± 7.5% (p = 0.024) for small intestine, while preserving PTV homogeneity and conformity. Importantly, the entire treatment planning time was within 3 minutes, with fluence optimization time decreased by an average of 82.6% after using deep learning prediction. The mean gamma passing rate under the 2%/2 mm criterion for the patient-specific IMRT QA achieved 97.37 ± 1.01%. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrated the clinical feasibility of the proposed HALO framework for cervical cancer radiotherapy in producing high-quality and deliverable IMRT plans. The proposed automated paradigm can serve as a stand-alone platform for treatment planning.
items.why: This study developed a hybrid automated deep learning-based plan optimization (HALO) framework for cervical cancer intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT), combining a fluence prediction network with Monte Carlo dose calculation, tested on 20 held-out patients with patient-specific quality assurance (QA) showing a 97.4% gamma passing rate, reduced bladder and small intestine dose, and planning time under 3 minutes versus the typical trial-and-error process. This is a concrete demonstration of clinically feasible, substantially faster automated radiotherapy planning with real dosimetric and QA verification, which is a meaningful advance in clinical AI for oncology even outside reproductive medicine specifically.
items.plain: Researchers built an AI system that can automatically design radiation treatment plans for cervical cancer in under 3 minutes, instead of the usual lengthy trial-and-error process done by human planners. The AI plans reduced radiation exposure to nearby organs like the bladder and intestine while passing standard safety checks, suggesting this could make high-quality cancer treatment planning faster and more consistent.

items.title: Head-to-head comparison of six commercial artificial intelligence algorithms for embryo ploidy risk stratification in 1000 PGT-A-tested blastocysts.
items.body: RESEARCH QUESTION: Do commercial artificial intelligence (AI)-based embryo assessment algorithms differ in their ability to stratify the risk of embryo ploidy, or do they converge towards a similar level of discrimination despite being developed for different clinical objectives? DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study conducted at a single IVF centre, including 1000 blastocysts from 273 patients treated between 2022 and 2023. Embryos were scored using six anonymized commercial AI models (three each of static- or video-based). Ploidy status was determined by trophectoderm biopsy followed by preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A). Performance was evaluated using multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curves (continuous scores). Euploidy enrichment across within-algorithm score strata and rank concordance (Kendall's τ-b) were assessed, with subgroup analyses by Asociación para el Estudio de la Biología de la Reproducción morphological grade and oocyte age. RESULTS: All six algorithms showed moderate discrimination between euploid and aneuploid embryos (area under the curve range 0.713-0.744, overlapping 95% CI), and their continuous scores were significantly associated with ploidy status (all P < 0.001). For each model, higher score strata were associated with progressive enrichment of euploid embryos, despite substantial overlap in score distributions between ploidy groups. Ranking concordance between algorithms was moderate, indicating that embryos prioritized by different systems frequently differed. These patterns were broadly consistent across morphological grades and maternal age strata. CONCLUSIONS: Across 1000 PGT-A-validated blastocysts, commercial AI embryo assessment algorithms converge towards a shared ceiling of ploidy risk stratification performance. These tools should therefore be interpreted as relative risk stratification systems rather than diagnostic tests. While AI scores may support embryo prioritization when PGT-A cannot be performed, limited concordance across algorithms indicates that the choice of algorithm can influence which embryos are prioritized.
items.why: This retrospective single-center cohort directly compared six commercial artificial intelligence (AI) embryo scoring algorithms against preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) ground truth in 1000 blastocysts, finding all six converged to similar moderate discrimination (AUC 0.713-0.744) but showed only moderate rank concordance with each other, meaning different algorithms would prioritize different embryos for transfer. This is a useful head-to-head benchmark showing that commercial embryo AI tools are not interchangeable and should be treated as relative risk stratifiers rather than diagnostic substitutes for PGT-A, a finding directly actionable for clinics choosing or combining these systems.
items.plain: Scientists tested six different commercial AI tools that score embryos for chromosomal normalcy against the gold-standard genetic test, using 1000 embryos from a single fertility clinic. All six tools performed similarly overall but often disagreed on which specific embryos looked best, showing that choosing one AI tool over another can change which embryo gets transferred, and that none of these tools should replace genetic testing when it's available.

items.title: Radiomics-Guided Automatic Delineation for Clinical Target Volume of Endometrial Cancer: Limited Sample Multicenter Study.
items.source: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
items.body: PURPOSE: The inconsistent delineation of the clinical target volume (CTV) in postoperative pelvic radiation therapy for endometrial carcinoma across centers poses a challenge for deep learning-based segmentation due to differing definitions of the internal target volume. This study aimed to develop an effective method to address multi-institutional variations in CTV delineation, even under the constraints of limited data availability. METHODS AND MATERIALS: A total of 207 simulated computed tomography cases of patients with endometrial cancer across 5 centers were retrospectively collected. Within each center, the data were divided into support, query, and test sets. Each center was sequentially designated as the target center for fine-tuning and testing, while the remaining 4 centers were used for model training to validate the superiority of the proposed method. In addition, 26 cases from an external center were used exclusively for fine-tuning and testing. Radiomics features were extracted to analyze differences in CTV delineation and images across centers. A random forest classifier was trained to identify the most important radiomics features. Using these features as guidance, a model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) strategy was applied to pretrain a 3-dimensional U-Net radiomics-guided MAML (MAML-r) model, which was subsequently fine-tuned on each target center's data. The performance of the proposed MAML-r method was compared with direct 3-dimensional U-Net training and transfer learning models. Evaluation metrics included the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), the 95th percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95), and the average symmetric surface distance (ASSD), supplemented by qualitative assessments from clinical experts using a 4-point scoring system. RESULTS: Eight important features were identified from a total of 107 radiomics features, which showed significant differences across centers (P < .01). The MAML-r model yielded meaningful results, achieving a mean ± SD DSC of 0.818 ± 0.058, a mean ± SD HD95 of 9.314 ± 3.648 mm, and a mean ± SD ASSD of 2.772 ± 1.090 mm. The model also earned an average blinded expert evaluation score of 3.24, significantly outperforming all other models. Notably, improved performance was observed in the external test cohort, with corresponding mean ± SD values for DSC, HD95, and ASSD of 0.886 ± 0.012, 5.203 ± 1.435 mm, and 1.512 ± 0.334 mm, respectively. Furthermore, the MAML-r model achieved the shortest mean ± SD CTV modification time of 3.8 ± 1.2 minutes. Given the variations in CTV contouring styles across centers and the limited sample size, the MAML-r model demonstrated superior performance and adaptability compared with the other models. CONCLUSIONS: This study introduces a novel MAML-r framework for few-shot, multicentric CTV segmentation tasks in postoperative pelvic radiation therapy for endometrial carcinoma, significantly mitigating performance degradation caused by interinstitutional variations in delineation styles and data scarcity. The proposed approach offers a promising solution to these persistent clinical challenges.
items.why: This multicenter retrospective study trained a model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) approach combined with radiomics features to guide 3D U-Net segmentation of clinical target volumes (CTV) for endometrial cancer radiotherapy across 5 centers plus an external site, achieving a Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.818-0.886 and outperforming standard transfer learning. The approach meaningfully addresses the real problem of inter-institutional variability in contouring, and the improved performance on the external test cohort is a genuine strength, though the dataset remains small and limited to CT-based segmentation rather than clinical outcomes.
items.plain: This study built an AI system that automatically draws the radiation treatment area for endometrial cancer patients, designed to work well even when different hospitals draw these areas slightly differently. The system performed better than standard methods and even improved on a hospital it had never seen before, which matters for standardizing radiation planning in gynecologic cancer care, though it only covers contouring, not outcomes like survival.

items.title: Fusing Tabular Features and Deep Learning for Fetal Heart Rate Analysis: A Clinically Interpretable Model for Fetal Compromise Detection.
items.body: OBJECTIVE: Cardiotocography (CTG) is commonly used to monitor fetal heart rate (FHR) and assess fetal well-being during labor. However, its effectiveness in reducing adverse outcomes remains limited due to low sensitivity and high false-positive rates. This study aims to develop an interpretable deep learning model that fuses FHR time series with tabular clinical features to improve prediction of fetal compromise (umbilical artery pH $< $ 7.05). METHODS: We introduce Fusion ResNet, a novel architecture combining residual convolutional networks for FHR signal processing with a parallel neural network for tabular features. The model was trained and internally validated on a private dataset of 9,887 FHR recordings. External validation was performed on the open-access CTU-UHB dataset comprising 552 recordings. Model interpretability was evaluated using Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and Gradient-Weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). RESULTS: Fusion ResNet achieved a mean area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.77 during internal cross-validation and a state-of-the-art AUC of 0.84 on the CTU-UHB dataset, outperforming existing deep learning approaches. SHAP analysis identified key clinical features contributing to predictions, while Grad-CAM highlighted salient FHR patterns linked to fetal compromise. CONCLUSION: The proposed model enhances predictive accuracy while providing clinically meaningful explanations, enabling more transparent and reliable CTG interpretation. SIGNIFICANCE: This work demonstrates the potential of interpretable deep learning to improve fetal monitoring by integrating multimodal data, supporting timely and informed decision-making in obstetric care.
items.why: This study developed Fusion ResNet, a deep learning architecture combining a residual convolutional network for fetal heart rate (FHR) time series with tabular clinical features to predict fetal compromise defined by umbilical artery pH below 7.05, achieving area under the curve (AUC) 0.77 internally and 0.84 on an external dataset (CTU-UHB), with interpretability via Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). The genuine external validation and interpretability tools are meaningful strengths for a notoriously noisy signal like cardiotocography (CTG), though clinical adoption would still require prospective trial evidence tying predictions to actual intervention and outcome improvement.
items.plain: Researchers built an AI model that combines fetal heart rate patterns during labor with other clinical information to predict when a baby may be in danger, and it performed better on a completely separate, independent dataset than earlier methods. The model also explains which features drove its predictions, which is useful for doctors trying to trust and understand the tool, but it still needs to be tested in real clinical use to know if it actually improves outcomes.

items.title: OsteoCHAT: real-world patient evaluation and benchmarking of a guideline-grounded osteoporosis chatbot.
items.body: UNLABELLED: Patients with osteoporosis have information needs that routine care inconsistently addresses. In this multicenter real-world evaluation, the LLM-based, guideline-grounded chatbot OsteoCHAT showed high participant acceptability and achieved expert-rated answer quality comparable to general-purpose LLMs. Despite challenges in complex treatment and safety-related topics, guideline-grounded chatbots may represent useful educational adjuncts. PURPOSE: Patients with osteoporosis have information needs that routine care inconsistently addresses. Guideline-grounded chatbots may offer scalable educational support METHODS: We developed OsteoCHAT, a retrieval-augmented conversational system based on the current German osteoporosis guideline, and conducted a multicenter evaluation at seven centers in Germany. Participants interacted with OsteoCHAT, provided real-time feedback on individual responses, and completed a standardized questionnaire assessing usability, comprehensibility, usefulness, trust, perceived quality, and preference over conventional internet search. In parallel, OsteoCHAT was benchmarked against three general-purpose large language models (LLMs) using ten osteoporosis frequently asked questions derived from the BfO patient guideline as the gold standard. Five clinical experts independently rated these responses across five domains, each scored 0-3. RESULTS: Overall, 1,075 question-answer interactions were recorded. Of 389 individually rated responses, 379 (97.4%) received positive feedback. Among 217 complete questionnaire responses, 84.3% rated answers as easily understandable, 79.8% found OsteoCHAT easy to use, 77.2% perceived time savings, and 78.7% considered it a useful addition to existing educational materials. Trust was comparatively lower (64.7% agreement). Blinded expert benchmarking showed acceptable-to-high-quality responses across all LLMs (median total scores 14/15 for Gemini, ChatGPT, and OsteoCHAT and 13/15 for Meta AI), with expert-identified weaknesses mainly concerning pharmacological treatment indication and communication of adverse and rare safety-critical events. CONCLUSION: OsteoCHAT demonstrated high user acceptability and usability in a real-world multicenter evaluation, was rated as a valuable addition to existing educational materials, and achieved expert-rated response quality comparable to general-purpose LLMs, although limitations in safety communication were identified across all examined systems.
items.why: This multicenter real-world evaluation deployed OsteoCHAT, a retrieval-augmented, guideline-grounded large language model (LLM) chatbot, to 1,075 real patient-chatbot interactions across seven German centers, finding 97.4% positive feedback and expert-rated answer quality comparable to general-purpose LLMs, with identified weaknesses in pharmacological and safety-related topics. Real deployment with patient feedback and expert benchmarking against general LLMs, rather than another rubric-only simulation, makes this a more substantive contribution to this beat, though trust scores were comparatively lower and no control group or outcome measure beyond satisfaction was used.
items.plain: Researchers built a chatbot grounded in official osteoporosis treatment guidelines and had real patients use it across seven medical centers in Germany, collecting over a thousand actual question-and-answer interactions. Patients mostly liked it and found it as good as general AI chatbots, but experts found it struggled with explaining medication risks and rare safety issues, which matters because this was tested on real patients rather than simulated cases.

items.title: Effectiveness of a Chatbot-Based Hypertension Management Program on Selected Outcomes Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
items.body: AIM: Hypertension remains poorly controlled among older adults because self-care support between outpatient visits is rarely sustained. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a chatbot-based hypertension management program on knowledge, health behaviors, medication adherence, blood pressure control, and selected biomarkers among community-dwelling older adults with hypertension. DESIGN: Quasi-experimental study. METHODS: A two-group pretest-posttest design was conducted in two healthcare settings: the experimental group was recruited from a tertiary hospital outpatient department and the control group from a primary care health promoting hospital. Sixty-eight participants were recruited using consecutive sampling and assigned to an experimental group (n = 34) or a control group (n = 34). The experimental group received a 12-week chatbot-based program combining education, behavioral monitoring, and lifestyle counseling. The control group received usual care using a hypertension education manual. Outcomes were assessed at baseline and after 12 weeks. RESULTS: The experimental group showed improvements in hypertension-related knowledge, health behaviors, medication adherence, and blood pressure control. The control group showed no improvement in systolic and a rise in diastolic blood pressure. After adjustment for baseline values and for the demographic characteristics that differed at baseline, the experimental group demonstrated better knowledge (p = 0.002), health behaviors (p = 0.018), medication adherence (p< 0.001) and blood pressure control than the control group (adjusted systolic 127.43 compared to 135.80 mmHg, p = 0.009; adjusted diastolic 69.61 compared to 80.36 mmHg, p< 0.001). No significant adjusted between-group differences in biomarkers were observed. CONCLUSION: A chatbot-supported hypertension management program was associated with better self-management and blood pressure control among community-dwelling older adults, although the non-randomized design and recruitment from different settings mean that the findings are preliminary. Longer follow-up is needed to determine effects on biological indicators. Randomized designs are recommended in future studies to strengthen the generalizability of the findings.
items.why: This quasi-experimental pretest-posttest study tested a 12-week chatbot-based hypertension management program against usual care in 68 community-dwelling older adults, finding significant improvements in knowledge, medication adherence, and blood pressure control (adjusted systolic 127.4 vs 135.8 mmHg) in the intervention group. The measured effect on a hard clinical endpoint, blood pressure, is a meaningful step beyond typical rubric-based chatbot studies, though the non-randomized design with recruitment from different healthcare settings limits causal certainty.
items.plain: This study tested a chatbot program that helped older adults manage high blood pressure through education and reminders over 12 weeks, comparing it to a group that just got a standard pamphlet. The chatbot group showed real improvements in blood pressure readings and medication habits, which is a genuine health outcome rather than just a quality score, though the study was not a randomized trial so the comparison could be influenced by other differences between the groups.

items.title: Artificial intelligence and vascular surgeons in patient communication: A comparative analysis of intelligibility and clinical appropriateness in acute deep vein thrombosis.
items.body: ObjectiveEffective patient communication is critical in acute deep vein thrombosis (DVT) management. This study evaluated and compared the intelligibility and clinical appropriateness of patient-directed explanations for acute DVT generated by vascular surgeons versus a diverse panel of large language models (LLMs), using a balanced, unit-matched design.MethodsIn this observational, cross-sectional study, 11 board-certified vascular surgeons and 11 distinct, independently developed LLMs each produced one response to a standardized acute DVT vignette in Spanish. Responses were blinded and scored using an 8-item clinical appropriateness grid (two independent graders, consensus) and five validated Spanish readability indices. Central tendency was assessed with Mann-Whitney U tests; dispersion was assessed descriptively (coefficient of variation, range) and, exploratorily, with Brown-Forsythe tests.ResultsClinical appropriateness did not differ significantly between groups (median 7/8 in both;= 0.258), dispersion was descriptively far smaller for LLMs (SD 0.40 vs 1.92; coefficient of variation 5.9% vs 32.5%). LLM responses were more readable on three of four content-complexity indices (Fernández-Huerta, Gutiérrez de Polini, Szigriszt-Pazos; all< 0.02) and required a numerically lower educational grade level (Crawford 5.4 vs 6.1;= 0.075). Readability dispersion was descriptively far lower for LLMs (Fernández-Huerta range 31 vs 200 points; coefficient of variation 15% vs 181%), driven in the surgeon cohort by a single response that fell far outside the interpretable range; formal variance tests did not reach significance at this sample size. LLM responses were longer (median 903 vs 354 words;= 0.003) and took longer to read (4.5 vs 1.8 min;< 0.001). Neither group addressed screening for silent pulmonary embolism. Free-versus-premium comparisons were model-specific rather than uniform.ConclusionCurrent-generation LLMs matched board-certified surgeons in clinical completeness and produced more readable, descriptively far more consistent patient-facing explanations, without the communication failures observed in a minority of human responses. Both cohorts share an important, guideline-adjacent counseling gap.
items.why: This observational cross-sectional study directly compared patient-facing explanations of acute deep vein thrombosis (DVT) from 11 board-certified vascular surgeons against 11 distinct large language models (LLMs), blinded and scored on clinical appropriateness and readability, finding no significant difference in appropriateness (median 7/8 both) but substantially lower variability and higher readability in LLM responses. This is a genuine clinician comparator study, the kind that is more discriminating and useful for this beat, though the sample of surgeon responses is small and the setting is Spanish-language and single-vignette.
items.plain: This study had real vascular surgeons and various AI chatbots each write an explanation of a blood clot diagnosis for patients, then had graders blindly compare them. The AI responses were judged just as medically appropriate as the surgeons' explanations, and were more consistently clear and readable, though both groups missed mentioning a key related risk, which is a notable finding because it directly pits AI against real doctors rather than just scoring AI answers alone.

scored.title: Embedding LLMs in the patient portal to summarize acute minor illness information: a three-arm experimental study.
scored.why: This three-arm experimental study embedded two frontier large language models (LLMs) into a primary care patient portal to generate plain-language summaries of acute illness information, finding significantly higher comprehension scores, portal engagement, and self-management adherence versus standard portal access, plus a 61% lower odds of unnecessary return visits (odds ratio 0.34). This is a rare randomized comparison with a hard utilization endpoint and clinician-audited safety data, making it one of the more substantive patient-facing LLM evaluations this cycle.

scored.title: Deep Time-to-Event Models for Intrapartum Fetal Monitoring.
scored.why: This study reframes intrapartum fetal heart rate monitoring (cardiotocography, CTG) as a time-to-event prediction problem rather than assuming a fixed pre-delivery window, developing a deep learning model called Marked DeepHit that jointly predicts imminent delivery and fetal acidosis, achieving test-set area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.837 to 0.935 at 6 and 12 hours into labor, with validation at a second external site. The external validation and the novel time-to-event framing that avoids the unrealistic assumption of known delivery timing make this a methodologically meaningful advance toward real-world deployable intrapartum monitoring, though it remains a proof-of-principle rather than a deployed clinical tool.

scored.title: CTG-FRAME: development and validation of a multi‑modal deep learning for intrapartum escalation support and severe fetal acidemia prediction.
scored.why: CTG-FRAME is a multi-module deep learning framework for predicting severe fetal acidemia from cardiotocography (CTG) signals, trained and cross-validated on the CTU-UHB dataset (n=552) and externally tested on a separate multicenter cohort (SPaM, n=300), achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.888 with sensitivity 0.85 and specificity 0.964, and showing preserved calibration without retuning on external data. This is a genuine external validation of an intrapartum decision-support tool addressing a well-known clinical problem, high false-positive burden in fetal monitoring, making it one of the stronger obstetric AI entries this week, though the acidemia prevalence differs notably between cohorts.

scored.title: Feasibility and Reproducibility of a Structure-Guided Deep Learning Model for Automatic Detection of the Standard Sagittal Plane in First-Trimester Nuchal Translucency Assessment Using 3D Ultrasound.
scored.why: This prospective study developed 3D MSP-net, a convolutional neural network (CNN) that automatically extracts the mid-sagittal plane (MSP) from 3D ultrasound for first-trimester nuchal translucency (NT) measurement, achieving a 91.6% success rate comparable to manual methods and superior to a commercial rule-based system, with nuchal translucency measurements statistically equivalent to manual assessment and reproducible on external validation. The robustness across maternal body mass index and scan angles plus genuine external validation make this a credible step toward reducing operator dependence in a widely performed screening test.

scored.title: Evaluating the impact of social determinants of health on model performance and fairness in artificial intelligence for glaucoma progression prediction.
scored.why: This multicenter study of 63,268 glaucoma patients across 12 centers tested whether adding community-level social determinants of health (SDoH, such as area deprivation and rural-urban location) to an XGBoost model predicting progression to glaucoma surgery improved algorithmic fairness, finding reduced generalized equalized odds (GEO, a fairness metric comparing error rates across subgroups) at the internal site and one external site but not at two demographically different external sites. The large multicenter design with external validation is a methodological strength, and the finding that fairness gains do not transfer across sites is directly relevant to anyone deploying prediction models across health systems.

scored.title: MADE: leveraging informative missingness and temporal evaluation for electronic health record-based deterioration prediction in general wards.
scored.why: This study developed Masked-Attention-based timestamp-wise Data Embedding (MADE), a missingness-aware transformer model for predicting deterioration in general hospital wards, validated across one internal and two external cohorts, achieving area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.966/0.902/0.825 for major adverse events and 0.934/0.874/0.776 for sepsis, with the no-imputation configuration outperforming standard imputation methods. The multi-site external validation and the finding that missingness itself carries predictive signal are methodologically notable, though calibration degraded at higher risk levels, suggesting site-specific recalibration is needed before deployment.

scored.title: The Building and Application of a Machine Learning Model on Predicting Euploid Blastocysts in IVF Treatments Without PGT-A.
scored.why: This study built a logistic regression-based machine learning model using preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) results, morphokinetic development, morphology, and maternal age to predict blastocyst euploidy, achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.877 on an independent validation set and a lower false positive rate than Gardner grading or KIDScore D5; frozen embryo transfer outcomes improved when embryos were selected by the model versus conventional morphology grading. The comparison against established clinical grading systems and the reported improvement in a real treatment outcome make this more actionable than typical embryo-selection models, though details on study design and cohort size are sparse.

scored.title: Foundation model-powered deep learning of endometrial histology for predicting the cumulative live birth of an in vitro fertilization cycle.
scored.why: This study compared an end-to-end convolutional network against a frozen foundation model feature extractor (UNI2-h) for predicting cumulative live birth from endometrial histology images in in vitro fertilization (IVF) patients, finding the foundation model approach generalized better to an external phase-based test cohort (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUROC, of 0.90 versus near-random for the standard model) despite lower performance on the internal outcome-based task. The divergence between internal and external performance highlights a genuine generalization problem relevant to anyone building histology-based prediction tools, and the finding that pretrained foundation models transfer better is a useful methodological signal even though absolute performance (AUROC 0.74 internally) remains modest for clinical use.

scored.title: A hybrid deep learning framework for automated treatment planning in cervical cancer radiotherapy.
scored.why: This study developed a hybrid automated deep learning-based plan optimization (HALO) framework for cervical cancer intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT), combining a fluence prediction network with Monte Carlo dose calculation, tested on 20 held-out patients with patient-specific quality assurance (QA) showing a 97.4% gamma passing rate, reduced bladder and small intestine dose, and planning time under 3 minutes versus the typical trial-and-error process. This is a concrete demonstration of clinically feasible, substantially faster automated radiotherapy planning with real dosimetric and QA verification, which is a meaningful advance in clinical AI for oncology even outside reproductive medicine specifically.

scored.title: Head-to-head comparison of six commercial artificial intelligence algorithms for embryo ploidy risk stratification in 1000 PGT-A-tested blastocysts.
scored.why: This retrospective single-center cohort directly compared six commercial artificial intelligence (AI) embryo scoring algorithms against preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A) ground truth in 1000 blastocysts, finding all six converged to similar moderate discrimination (AUC 0.713-0.744) but showed only moderate rank concordance with each other, meaning different algorithms would prioritize different embryos for transfer. This is a useful head-to-head benchmark showing that commercial embryo AI tools are not interchangeable and should be treated as relative risk stratifiers rather than diagnostic substitutes for PGT-A, a finding directly actionable for clinics choosing or combining these systems.

scored.source: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
scored.title: Radiomics-Guided Automatic Delineation for Clinical Target Volume of Endometrial Cancer: Limited Sample Multicenter Study.
scored.why: This multicenter retrospective study trained a model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) approach combined with radiomics features to guide 3D U-Net segmentation of clinical target volumes (CTV) for endometrial cancer radiotherapy across 5 centers plus an external site, achieving a Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.818-0.886 and outperforming standard transfer learning. The approach meaningfully addresses the real problem of inter-institutional variability in contouring, and the improved performance on the external test cohort is a genuine strength, though the dataset remains small and limited to CT-based segmentation rather than clinical outcomes.

scored.title: Fusing Tabular Features and Deep Learning for Fetal Heart Rate Analysis: A Clinically Interpretable Model for Fetal Compromise Detection.
scored.why: This study developed Fusion ResNet, a deep learning architecture combining a residual convolutional network for fetal heart rate (FHR) time series with tabular clinical features to predict fetal compromise defined by umbilical artery pH below 7.05, achieving area under the curve (AUC) 0.77 internally and 0.84 on an external dataset (CTU-UHB), with interpretability via Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) and Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM). The genuine external validation and interpretability tools are meaningful strengths for a notoriously noisy signal like cardiotocography (CTG), though clinical adoption would still require prospective trial evidence tying predictions to actual intervention and outcome improvement.

scored.title: OsteoCHAT: real-world patient evaluation and benchmarking of a guideline-grounded osteoporosis chatbot.
scored.why: This multicenter real-world evaluation deployed OsteoCHAT, a retrieval-augmented, guideline-grounded large language model (LLM) chatbot, to 1,075 real patient-chatbot interactions across seven German centers, finding 97.4% positive feedback and expert-rated answer quality comparable to general-purpose LLMs, with identified weaknesses in pharmacological and safety-related topics. Real deployment with patient feedback and expert benchmarking against general LLMs, rather than another rubric-only simulation, makes this a more substantive contribution to this beat, though trust scores were comparatively lower and no control group or outcome measure beyond satisfaction was used.

scored.title: Effectiveness of a Chatbot-Based Hypertension Management Program on Selected Outcomes Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults: A Quasi-Experimental Study.
scored.why: This quasi-experimental pretest-posttest study tested a 12-week chatbot-based hypertension management program against usual care in 68 community-dwelling older adults, finding significant improvements in knowledge, medication adherence, and blood pressure control (adjusted systolic 127.4 vs 135.8 mmHg) in the intervention group. The measured effect on a hard clinical endpoint, blood pressure, is a meaningful step beyond typical rubric-based chatbot studies, though the non-randomized design with recruitment from different healthcare settings limits causal certainty.

scored.title: Artificial intelligence and vascular surgeons in patient communication: A comparative analysis of intelligibility and clinical appropriateness in acute deep vein thrombosis.
scored.why: This observational cross-sectional study directly compared patient-facing explanations of acute deep vein thrombosis (DVT) from 11 board-certified vascular surgeons against 11 distinct large language models (LLMs), blinded and scored on clinical appropriateness and readability, finding no significant difference in appropriateness (median 7/8 both) but substantially lower variability and higher readability in LLM responses. This is a genuine clinician comparator study, the kind that is more discriminating and useful for this beat, though the sample of surgeon responses is small and the setting is Spanish-language and single-vignette.

scored.title: Intervention Without Borders - an Automated Self-Guided AI-Enhanced Psychoeducation Intervention for Dementia Caregivers: Parallel-Group Randomized Waitlist-Controlled Trial.
scored.why: A randomized waitlist-controlled trial tested a fully automated, AI-enhanced psychoeducation intervention (including a counseling chatbot) for 274 dementia caregivers across 43 countries, finding significant one-month improvements in depression (Patient Health Questionnaire-9), burden, and positive gains versus waitlist control. This is a genuine randomized comparison with a validated psychiatric outcome measure, which is more rigorous than typical patient-facing chatbot studies even though the chatbot is one component of a larger digital intervention.

scored.title: Orchestrator multi-agent clinical decision support system for secondary headache diagnosis in primary care.
scored.why: This study built an orchestrator-specialist multi-agent large language model (LLM) system that decomposes secondary headache red-flag diagnosis into seven guideline-aligned sub-agents, evaluating it against single-LLM baselines on 90 expert-validated cases across five open-source models, with the multi-agent design improving F1 score especially for smaller models. The evaluation, though modest in sample size and retrospective, demonstrates a concrete architectural approach to making LLM-based clinical decision support more interpretable, which is relevant to primary care triage but lacks prospective or real-world deployment data.

scored.title: The importance of clinical context in evaluating algorithmic fairness: insights from a medication adherence prediction algorithm.
scored.why: This retrospective study of 34,697 heart failure patients evaluated a medication-nonadherence prediction algorithm for fairness, finding similar overall accuracy across socioeconomic and racial subgroups but higher false-positive rate ratios (RR 1.50 for low versus high neighborhood socioeconomic status, RR 2.05 for Black versus White patients), and argued that the clinical consequence of these errors, not accuracy alone, determines whether a deployment worsens disparities. The analysis is a clear, concrete illustration that equal accuracy can mask harmful subgroup-specific error patterns, a point directly useful for anyone evaluating clinical AI deployment for equity.

scored.title: The relative importance of neighborhood environment features in explaining preeclampsia risk using machine learning.
scored.why: Using a matched case-control cohort of 18,754 participants from two Philadelphia hospitals, this study applied XGBoost models and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) to rank 26 neighborhood-level features by importance in predicting preeclampsia, identifying community prevalence of obesity, hypertension, and short sleep duration as the top predictors. The large sample size and use of interpretability methods to surface actionable community-level targets make this a solid, if purely observational and non-interventional, contribution to obstetric risk modeling.

scored.title: Medical Counselling in Imminent Premature Birth: The Chatbot as Expert And Friend? A Pilot Study.
scored.why: In this pilot study, neonatologists rated ChatGPT-generated responses to prenatal counseling scenarios for imminent extremely preterm birth, finding high empathy ratings but gaps in nuance, contextual sensitivity, and emphasis on joint parent-clinician decision-making. The reproductive and obstetric setting and real clinician evaluation of counseling-relevant content make this more germane than typical readability audits, though it lacks a clinician-response comparator and is explicitly preliminary.

scored.title: Simplified vitrification-warming protocol in donor oocytes: artificial intelligence-based oocyte competence and clinical outcomes.
scored.why: This prospective randomized proof-of-concept study using sibling donor oocytes compared a simplified single-step vitrification-warming protocol against the conventional multistep protocol, finding comparable survival, fertilization, blastocyst, implantation, and ongoing pregnancy rates, with secondary artificial intelligence (AI)-based oocyte competence scoring showing no meaningful difference between protocols. The randomized sibling-oocyte design gives real internal validity for the protocol comparison, though the AI competence assessment here is used only as a secondary outcome measure rather than being the focus of validation.

scored.title: SPELL: A scalable NLP method using regular expressions and large language models for clinical information extraction.
scored.why: This study developed SPELL, a hybrid pipeline combining regular-expression-based text retrieval with locally hosted large language model (LLM) inference, and deployed it across 31 million clinical notes from eight hospitals spanning 1976-2024, achieving 92-98% exact-match accuracy on obstetric extraction tasks like estimated due dates and HELLP syndrome diagnosis while cutting processing time by over 70% compared to full-document LLM inference. The real multi-hospital scale and clinician-annotated benchmarking make this a credible demonstration of LLM-based information extraction infrastructure, though it is extraction from existing notes rather than patient-facing dialogue, so its relevance to patient communication research is indirect.

scored.title: Diagnostic accuracy of an artificial intelligence-based breast ultrasound tool in pregnant and lactating patients.
scored.why: This retrospective two-center study compared an artificial intelligence (AI)-based decision support tool against radiologist interpretation for breast ultrasound in 504 pregnant and lactating patients with 639 findings, finding comparable sensitivity (80% for both) but the AI tool recommended more biopsies for benign lesions before excluding out-of-scope findings. This is one of the few studies evaluating AI performance specifically in the pregnant and lactating population, a group typically excluded from AI validation studies, though the small number of malignancies (5) limits statistical confidence in the sensitivity estimate.

scored.title: Medical Counselling in Imminent Premature Birth: The Chatbot as Expert And Friend? A Pilot Study.
scored.why: In this pilot study, neonatologists rated ChatGPT-generated responses to prenatal counseling scenarios for imminent extremely preterm birth, finding high empathy ratings but gaps in nuance, contextual sensitivity, and emphasis on joint parent-clinician decision-making. The reproductive and obstetric setting and real clinician evaluation of counseling-relevant content make this more germane than typical readability audits, though it lacks a clinician-response comparator and is explicitly preliminary.

scored.title: From isolation to engagement: Chatbot-delivered narratives as a social surrogate for novice quitters and socially isolated smokers.
scored.why: In this experiment with 386 adult smokers, chatbot-delivered narrative messages significantly increased intentions to disclose smoking experiences and seek support from AI-powered programs compared to non-narrative or first-person narrative formats, with effects moderated by perceived social support. This is a genuine behavioral experiment measuring an effect of chatbot-delivered communication on patient engagement intentions, which is more substantive than typical rubric-based readability studies, though intentions rather than actual cessation outcomes limit its strength.

scored.title: Evaluating the Utility and Acceptability of an Artificial Intelligence-Powered Care Aid for Perioperative Patient Inquiries in Joint Arthroplasty Surgery.
scored.why: A prospective observational pilot study deployed a custom AI care aid answering real perioperative questions from 32 joint arthroplasty patients, finding high engagement and mixed but mostly positive satisfaction and comprehension ratings, though nearly a third found postoperative question resolution unsatisfactory. This is a genuine deployment on real patient queries with longitudinal follow-up, which is more informative than a typical rubric study, though it lacks a clinician comparator or control arm.

scored.title: Small language models in clinical medicine: a systematic review of performance, safety, and deployment feasibility.
scored.why: This systematic review assessed 11 studies of small language models (SLMs, language models with 4 billion parameters or fewer) in clinical tasks and found wide variability in a custom relative task score (RTS) against larger-model comparators, with hallucination and calibration rarely measured. It is useful for calibrating expectations about SLM deployment feasibility but offers no new clinical evidence, only a synthesis of a thin and heterogeneous literature.

scored.title: Development and temporal validation of a proof-of-concept artificial intelligence model for binary classification of cervical cotest.
scored.why: This single-center retrospective study trained ResNet50 and DenseNet201 convolutional neural networks (CNNs) on digitized ThinPrep cervical cotest images to classify dysplasia, reporting an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 96% and sensitivity of 93% on a small temporal validation cohort of 63 women, though all metrics were reported at the image-patch level rather than the patient level. The patch-level reporting and small temporal cohort limit the clinical interpretability of these numbers, and the authors themselves call for prospective multicenter patient-level validation before any implementation.

scored.title: Clinical feature grouping-based FT-Transformer for postpartum depression risk prediction: a longitudinal cohort study in perinatal women.
scored.why: Using longitudinal data from 1,138 perinatal women, this study developed Clinical-Group FT, a modified Feature Tokenizer plus Transformer (FT-Transformer) architecture that groups clinical variables before applying cross-attention, to predict postpartum depression (PPD) defined by an Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) score of 11 or higher, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.887 and F1 score of 0.734 on a held-out test set. The reasonably large single cohort and interpretability analysis are notable strengths, but the retrospective design and absence of external validation keep this in the incremental-but-solid category rather than practice-changing.

scored.title: Making medical AI benchmarks clinically interpretable: the case of mental health.
scored.why: This analysis stratified HealthBench, a 5000-conversation benchmark of large language model (LLM) responses to health-related queries, by clinical domain, finding that mental health subcategories like postpartum depression and suicidal crisis are unevenly represented and that domain-specific performance can diverge from aggregate scores by several percentage points. The methodological point about benchmark composition masking safety-relevant variation is useful context for evaluating LLM patient-facing tools, but this is rubric-based scoring without a clinician comparator or real patient deployment, keeping it in the routine range for this reader's research area.

scored.title: Whose Knowledge Counts in Labour? Obstetric Nurses Negotiating Clinical Judgement, Algorithmic Authority and Woman-Centred Care in Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Foetal Monitoring.
scored.why: This qualitative interpretive description study interviewed 18 obstetric nurses in Saudi Arabia about their experience working alongside an artificial intelligence-enhanced cardiotocography (CTG) system, finding that nurses often used system alerts to legitimize pre-existing clinical concerns and experienced asymmetric accountability when their judgment diverged from the algorithm. This is a real-world deployment account surfacing a genuine workflow and authority failure mode in intrapartum AI monitoring, though it is a small single-site qualitative study without quantitative outcome measures.

scored.title: Deep learning-based segmentation of human oocytes with cross-dataset evaluation.
scored.why: This study trained and compared four deep learning segmentation architectures, including a transformer-based model (SegFormer), to delineate oocyte subregions in microscopy images, evaluating cross-dataset generalization across multiple clinical sites with Dice similarity coefficients exceeding 99% for ooplasm and 86-94% for other regions after fine-tuning. The cross-site evaluation and domain adaptation are methodologically sound, but the work stops at segmentation accuracy without linking results to actual oocyte quality or clinical outcomes.

scored.title: DWI-derived intratumoral, peritumoral, and habitat features for preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis in early-stage cervical cancer using machine learning method.
