scored.why: This retrospective multicenter study built a radiomics-based machine learning model combining intratumoral, peritumoral, and habitat features from diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) to predict lymph node metastasis (LNM) in early-stage cervical cancer, with a fusion model reaching area under the curve (AUC) 0.837 on an internal test set. Despite involving four hospitals, this is still a retrospective radiomics study without prospective or truly external validation, placing it in the routine tier of imaging biomarker work.

scored.title: ChatGPT Health and ChatGPT Plus in Urogynecology: A Blinded Comparison of Response Quality, Guideline Concordance, and Safety.
scored.why: This blinded comparative study had five clinicians rate 48 responses from ChatGPT Health versus standard ChatGPT Plus to 24 urogynecology patient queries using the Quality Analysis of Medical Artificial Intelligence (QAMAI) instrument and a guideline-concordance checklist, finding ChatGPT Health scored modestly higher on clarity and completeness with comparable accuracy and safety. This is a within-model comparison without a clinician-generated comparator, but the reproductive health relevance and structured guideline-concordance assessment give it modest value above a typical chatbot rubric study.

scored.title: ChatGPT in the Development and Evaluation of Patient Satisfaction and Experience Questionnaires in Emergency Departments: A Feasibility Study.
scored.why: In this feasibility study, ChatGPT-generated and nurse-developed emergency department patient satisfaction questionnaires were compared on content validity index, Cronbach's alpha, and completion time, with the ChatGPT version showing comparable or better psychometric properties. This is a somewhat novel application, using LLMs for instrument development rather than direct patient communication, and includes a real comparator, but it concerns survey design rather than clinical communication or outcomes.

scored.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Chatbots in Genetic Counseling Practice: Current Uptake, Utilization, and Perspectives.
scored.why: This survey of 217 genetic counselors and students found that while 76.5% use general AI chatbots personally, only 8.8% use or recommend clinical genetics chatbots in practice, with lowest confidence in disclosing variants of uncertain significance. This provides real-world adoption data on clinician attitudes toward LLMs in a specialized counseling context, which is more informative than another rubric study, though it is self-reported survey data without outcome measurement.

scored.title: Evaluation of AI-Generated Surgical Decision Aids for Pelvic Floor Disorders.
scored.why: ChatGPT-generated decision aids for six urogynecologic treatment comparisons were rated by patients and physicians for understandability, reliability using a modified DISCERN instrument, and accuracy, finding high understandability but fair reliability and unfavorable accuracy on a third of topics. This is a cross-sectional rubric evaluation without a clinician-generated comparator, so it documents chatbot limitations but does not test real clinical impact.

scored.title: Guideline-grounded large language models for extracting genome-informed clinical recommendations from electronic health records.
scored.why: Researchers compared three large language models (LLMs) using baseline, guideline-aware, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) prompting to extract genome-informed clinical recommendations from electronic health record (EHR) notes, validated against manual chart review on only 18 patients and 34 documents, with the best F1 score reaching 0.81 using a small open-source model plus RAG. The sample size is too small to establish generalizability, though the direction (guideline grounding and retrieval improve extraction) is a reasonable signal for precision medicine informatics work.

scored.title: Assessing and improving data quality in health registries: a systematic review of dimensions, frameworks, and artificial intelligence-enabled approaches.
scored.why: This systematic review of 119 studies synthesizes how data quality in health registries has been conceptualized and assessed, noting that artificial intelligence (AI) methods are used selectively for tasks like anomaly detection and record linkage but implementation remains fragmented. It is a broad descriptive synthesis without new clinical evidence or a specific AI method evaluated against a real outcome, making it low priority for this reader's focus on AI application and deployment.

scored.title: CUI-Curate: a GraphRAG-based framework for automated clinical concept curation for NLP applications.
scored.why: This paper presents CUI-Curate, a graph-based retrieval-augmented generation (GraphRAG) framework that uses large language models (LLMs) to automatically build clinical concept sets from the Unified Medical Language System (UMLS), evaluated against manually curated sets for five clinical concepts. It shows a useful infrastructure tool for natural language processing (NLP) pipelines with strong recall against gold standards, but the evaluation is narrow (five concepts) and does not test downstream clinical impact.

scored.title: Benchmarking information extraction of physical activity from electronic health record with large language models: an natural language processing pipeline and comparative evaluation.
scored.why: This study benchmarked transformer-based and large language model (LLM)-based classifiers for extracting physical activity information from electronic health record (EHR) notes across three cohorts, with the best binary classification F1 reaching only 0.689 and multi-class performance modest (macro-F1 0.262). The authors themselves characterize this as an early feasibility study without downstream clinical evaluation, limiting its immediate relevance beyond establishing a benchmark pipeline.

scored.title: Translation readiness of model-based synthetic tabular data in healthcare: a systematic review and governance audit.
scored.why: This systematic review of 37 studies audited the translation-readiness of model-based synthetic tabular data (data generated by models like generative adversarial networks to mimic real patient records) in healthcare, finding that 92% relied solely on internal validation and few addressed privacy, fairness, or regulatory alignment. The authors propose a new reporting checklist, TRUST-SD, but the paper itself is a descriptive audit without new synthetic data generation or clinical evaluation, making it a background reference rather than a finding that changes practice.

scored.title: Cervical cancer survival analysis by integrating multi-omics data through an adaptive weighted deep neural network.
scored.why: This study introduces a deep neural network called AWMP that integrates multi-omics data to predict cervical cancer survival, reporting a 4.74% relative improvement in prognosis prediction over four comparator methods and identifying four genes and a B-cell subset associated with outcomes. The analysis is retrospective, lacks external validation, and the modest incremental gain over baseline methods limits its immediate clinical relevance.

scored.title: Transformer-Enhanced Deep CNN for Early Detection of Uterine Cancer in Histopathological Images.
scored.why: This study developed a transformer-enhanced deep convolutional neural network (TE-DCNN) combining convolutional and transformer architectures with attention mechanisms to classify four categories of uterine histopathology, reporting 99% accuracy, 0.97 sensitivity, and 0.98 specificity, outperforming standard convolutional neural network (CNN) and vision transformer (ViT) baselines. The near-perfect reported performance with no mention of external validation or multi-center testing raises concern about overfitting, and the lack of methodological detail on dataset size and splitting limits confidence in generalizability.

scored.title: Development and validation of a multimodal MRI habitat-based deep learning fusion model for predicting (252)Cf neutron therapy response in cervical cancer.
scored.why: This retrospective single-center study of 100 cervical cancer patients built a fusion model combining MRI habitat radiomics, deep learning features from a pre-trained ResNet50, and clinical-dosimetric parameters to predict response to californium-252 neutron brachytherapy, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.892 in a 30-patient validation split. The small sample size, single-center design, and lack of external validation limit confidence that this multimodal fusion approach would generalize beyond the training institution.

scored.title: Assessing the Accuracy, Completeness, and Reference Quality of GPT-4 and Google for Gynecologic Cancer Information: Comparative Quantitative Study.
scored.why: This study compared GPT-4 responses to Google search results across 21 standardized gynecologic cancer questions, with four blinded gynecologic oncology experts rating accuracy, completeness, and reference quality on Likert scales, finding GPT-4 outperformed Google on all three measures (median accuracy 6.00 vs 5.00, P=.04). The comparison is against a search engine rather than practicing clinicians, so it does not address the clinician-comparator or workflow-impact questions that would make this more actionable for this reader's research area.

scored.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence into Reproductive Medicine: A Predictive Algorithm for Noninvasive Live Birth Assessment.
scored.why: This retrospective single-center study trained four machine learning algorithms on 375 in vitro fertilization (IVF) cycles to predict live birth, with the best model (extreme gradient boosting, XGBoost) reaching an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.927 after Bayesian hyperparameter tuning and synthetic data augmentation. The authors themselves note that prospective external validation is required and that overestimation of treatment success is a risk, which places this in the routine category of unvalidated single-center prediction models common in this literature.

scored.title: Deep Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms for Cervical Cancer Segmentation on MRI: A Systematic Review.
scored.why: This systematic review following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines evaluated 30 studies of deep learning and machine learning for cervical cancer segmentation on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), reporting Dice similarity coefficients ranging from 0.60 to 0.93 but rating overall evidence certainty as low using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework due to heterogeneity and limited external validation. This is a methodologically rigorous review of a technically mature but clinically unproven segmentation application, placing it in the lower-priority tail for a reader tracking validated clinical AI.

scored.title: Clustering of non-invasive biomarkers to distinguish phenotype-related response differences in women with PCOS after the 16-week Nordic interval training intervention: A prospective cohort study.
scored.why: This prospective cohort study used extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to identify key biomarkers of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) in a large dataset, then applied clustering algorithms to 80 women completing a 16-week Nordic interval training intervention to identify phenotype-related exercise response patterns, with modest cluster stability (Jaccard index 0.45). The machine learning here is exploratory feature selection and unsupervised clustering rather than a validated clinical prediction or decision tool, and the moderate cluster stability limits confidence in the phenotype groupings described.

scored.title: Machine learning-based analysis of factors associated with clinical pregnancy in vitrified-warmed single euploid embryo transfer cycles.
scored.why: A retrospective cohort of 4300 vitrified-warmed single euploid embryo transfer cycles used gradient-boosted and ensemble machine learning models to identify predictors of clinical pregnancy, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.76 to 0.78 across algorithms and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) for interpretability. The identified predictors (age, anti-Mullerian hormone, endometrial thickness) largely recapitulate known clinical risk factors, and without external validation this adds little beyond existing clinical heuristics.

scored.title: Multiparametric MRI Radiomics-Based Interpretable Machine Learning Model for the Prediction of Lymphovascular Space Invasion in Endometrial Cancer.
scored.why: A two-center retrospective study built six machine learning models combining multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics with clinical markers to predict lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI) in endometrial cancer, with the best neural network model reaching validation AUC of 0.803. This is a fairly typical radiomics-plus-clinical-feature model without prospective or multi-institutional external validation beyond the two training sites, limiting its immediate clinical impact.

scored.title: Radiomic prediction of substantial LVSI in endometrial cancer using reduced field of view DWI- a feasibility study.
scored.why: This single-to-dual-center feasibility study compared radiomics models built on reduced field-of-view diffusion-weighted imaging (rFOV DWI) versus conventional DWI for predicting substantial lymphovascular space invasion (LVSI) in endometrial cancer, with internal AUC around 0.89-0.90 but external AUC dropping to 0.74. The marked performance drop on external testing despite harmonization efforts is a useful cautionary data point about generalizability, though the small sample size (206 total) limits broader conclusions.

scored.title: Prenatal serotonin reuptake inhibitor exposure and maternal depression symptoms are associated with altered fetal brain and placental development.
scored.why: This observational cohort study compared fetal brain and placental MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) measures between serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SRI) exposed and unexposed pregnancies, using deep learning only as a segmentation tool to quantify brain volumes rather than as the object of study. The finding that SRI exposure and maternal depression severity both associate with altered fetal hippocampal volume and cortical folding is clinically interesting for perinatal psychiatry, but the AI component is incidental and the design is retrospective observational without a prospective or externally validated model to evaluate.

scored.title: Leveraging Machine Learning to Uncover Ethnic-Specific Predictors of Maternal Postpartum Depression.
scored.why: This study applied random forest machine learning to a large national survey dataset (Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System, PRAMS, N=39,637) to identify ethnic-specific predictors of postpartum depression (PPD), reporting cross-validation area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.65 that dropped substantially on the held-out test set. The modest and degrading performance limits clinical utility, and the contribution is mainly descriptive risk-factor identification rather than a validated predictive tool.

scored.title: Artificial Intelligence Chatbots as Sources of Cancer Pain Information: A Comparative Evaluation of Quality, Transparency, and Readability.
scored.why: This cross-sectional study compared four AI chatbots (ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, Perplexity) on quality and readability of cancer pain information using standard rubrics (DISCERN, Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP), Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmark, Global Quality Score (GQS)) scored by two clinicians, finding model differences in transparency and readability but no clinical accuracy assessment. Without a clinician-generated comparator or a measured patient outcome, this is routine rubric-scoring work rather than something that changes practice.

scored.title: Quality and clinical implications of AI chatbot responses to common patient questions about total knee arthroplasty: a multidimensional comparative study.
scored.why: This cross-sectional study had seven orthopedic specialists blindly rate responses from nine chatbots to total knee arthroplasty (TKA) frequently asked questions using several validated quality rubrics, finding significant differences between models on quality, usability and transparency scales. The study only compares chatbots against each other with rubric scores and lacks a clinician-generated comparator or any measured patient outcome, making it routine for this beat.

scored.title: Large language models' performance in answering common patient questions about colonoscopy: an expert-based evaluation.
scored.why: This comparative observational study had 40 gastroenterologists rate ChatGPT-4 and Google Bard responses to 11 colonoscopy-related patient questions using a rubric across accuracy, applicability, comprehensiveness, and communication, finding ChatGPT-4 significantly outperformed Bard on all domains. This is another rubric-based large language model (LLM) comparison without a real clinician-generated comparator or measured patient outcome, placing it in the routine tier for this beat.

scored.title: Large language models in Hidradenitis suppurativa: strong empathy, weak exposome awareness.
scored.why: This blinded cross-sectional study had three dermatologists rate responses from five large language models (LLMs) to 47 simulated hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) consultations across six domains, finding high empathy and understandability scores but poor exposome awareness. Without a clinician-generated comparator or measured patient outcome, this remains a routine rubric-based benchmarking study for this beat despite its reasonably large case set and good inter-rater reliability.

scored.title: Exploratory Analysis of the Digital Health Gender Paradox in Consumer-Facing Digital Health Technology Adoption: Cross-Sectional Survey Study.
scored.why: This cross-sectional survey of 416 adults examines gender differences in digital health technology adoption using the Capability, Opportunity, Motivation-Behavior (COM-B) model, finding women have lower adjusted odds ratio (aOR 0.32) of chatbot use despite higher digital literacy. It touches on conversational agents only as one of several technologies studied and reports no communication quality or clinical outcome data, so its relevance to the LLM-patient beat is marginal.

scored.title: Quality of Tinnitus Information From Generative AI Systems and Web Search: An Expert‑Rated Comparative Study.
scored.why: Six generative AI systems and Google Search were compared by expert raters on tinnitus information quality using the QAMAI framework, finding OpenEvidence scored highest but with the lowest readability (postgraduate level), while general LLMs were more readable but lower quality. This reveals an inverse relationship between expert-rated quality and accessibility across platforms, useful context but still a routine comparative rubric study without clinician-patient interaction data.

scored.title: Readability, Quality, Understandability, and Actionability of ChatGPT Generated GI Patient Education Versus AGA Patient Center.
scored.why: This cross-sectional study compared ChatGPT-generated gastrointestinal patient education against American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) materials using Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, DISCERN, and Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT), finding comparable quality and understandability but significantly higher reading level for ChatGPT. The comparator here is a professional society resource rather than a clinician's direct response, so it is a modest step above a pure rubric study but still routine for this beat.

scored.title: Evaluating generative AI responses at the 3-month timepoint following total knee arthroplasty.
scored.why: Ten orthopedic surgeons rated responses from four generative AI models (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Grok) to postoperative total knee arthroplasty (TKA) questions on a 1-4 scale, finding Gemini most consistent and highest rated. This is a routine multi-model comparison rated by clinicians rather than a direct clinician-versus-AI comparison or patient outcome measure, so it is informative but not field-changing.

scored.title: Evaluation of the performance of large language models in the management of hip and knee osteoarthritis: analysis of EULAR 2023 recommendations.
scored.why: Three large language models (LLMs) were scored against 2023 European League Against Rheumatism (EULAR) osteoarthritis guideline recommendations on informational quality, reliability, usability, readability, and semantic similarity, with DeepSeek-R1 outperforming Gemini 2.5 Flash and ChatGPT-5 on most measures. There is no clinician comparator or patient outcome, just a rubric-based benchmark of guideline concordance, which is routine for this beat.

scored.title: Evaluation of the applicability of AI chatbots in addressing health management issues for living kidney donors.
scored.why: Four chatbots (ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, Copilot, Bard) were scored by six experts on accuracy, integrity, comprehensibility, and operability for living kidney donor health questions, with ChatGPT-4 performing best. This is another rubric-based comparison across models without a clinician benchmark or patient outcome, typical for this beat.

scored.title: Customized Education Sheets Generated by ChatGPT Improve Parental Visit Satisfaction and Procedural Knowledge Prior to Pediatric Cardiac Catheterization.
scored.why: A prospective single-center quality improvement study had ChatGPT-4 generate reading-level-tailored education sheets for 26 families before pediatric cardiac catheterization, finding modest but statistically significant improvements in parental understanding and satisfaction via Likert scores. The study lacks a control group and uses parametric statistics on ordinal data, a limitation also raised by an accompanying critique letter, limiting causal inference despite being a real clinical deployment.

scored.title: Understandability and Actionability of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Lymphedema Education Material in Patients Undergoing Breast Cancer Surgery: Expert Evaluation.
scored.why: Ten experts evaluated ChatGPT-4-generated lymphedema education material for breast cancer surgery patients using the Patient Education Materials Evaluation Tool and Global Quality Scale, finding high understandability, actionability, and readability scores in Turkish. This is an expert rubric assessment without patient testing, clinician comparator, or outcome measurement, making it routine evidence for this beat.

scored.title: Evaluation of artificial intelligence-based patient education models for irritable bowel syndrome.
scored.why: Two large language models (LLMs), ChatGPT-4 and Gemini-1, were compared on comprehensiveness, accuracy, readability, and empathy for 39 irritable bowel syndrome frequently asked questions, with Gemini scoring slightly higher comprehensiveness and ChatGPT rated more empathetic, though both produced difficult-to-read content. This is another rubric-based model-versus-model comparison without clinician benchmarking or patient-facing evaluation, typical of routine evidence on this beat.

scored.title: The clinician-artificial intelligence scientist: a proposed career pathway in medicine.
scored.why: This is a Viewpoint proposing a new career pathway, the clinician-artificial intelligence (AI) scientist, that would blend clinical and technical AI expertise, but it presents no original data or evaluation. It is a commentary on workforce development rather than a study that would change clinical practice or AI evaluation standards.

scored.title: Posthumous health data donation: an emerging framework for equitable healthcare AI.
scored.why: This perspective piece proposes posthumous health data donation as a mechanism to build more representative datasets for healthcare artificial intelligence (AI), arguing that death reduces the ethical harms associated with using personal health data. It is a conceptual and policy proposal without empirical data, evaluation, or deployment, so it has limited direct relevance to this reader's technical or clinical interests.

scored.title: Equity-by-design for socially assistive robots as digital health tools.
scored.why: This Perspective proposes an equity-by-design framework for socially assistive robots (SARs) in digital health, built from narrative synthesis rather than empirical testing. It offers a conceptual checklist for designers and policymakers but includes no deployment data or outcome evaluation relevant to clinical AI practice.

scored.title: A pilot evaluation of ChatGPT-4o-assisted hypothesis generation for exploring potential links between fungal biology and cervical cancer.
scored.why: This pilot study used ChatGPT-4o to generate 55 speculative research hypotheses linking fungal biology to cervical cancer, with three author-evaluators rating hypothesis quality and inter-rater reliability quantified by intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC); no comparison to human-generated hypotheses or alternative models was included. The work is purely exploratory brainstorming with no experimental validation, limited methodological rigor, and no clinical or translational endpoint.

scored.title: Liquid biopsy for early detection and biomarker applications in gynecological cancers: current status and future directions.
scored.why: This is a structured narrative review synthesizing liquid biopsy approaches, including circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), circulating tumor cells (CTCs), and multi-omics signatures, across gynecologic cancers, concluding that no assay has regulatory clearance and most evidence derives from retrospective designs. The review contains no artificial intelligence or algorithmic component and functions as a synthesis of molecular diagnostics literature rather than a clinical AI or reproductive AI study.

scored.title: Bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identify tumor-specific epithelial PSAT1 as a ferroptosis-associated therapeutic target in cervical cancer.
scored.why: Using bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing plus machine learning, this study nominated PSAT1 as a ferroptosis-related therapeutic target in cervical adenocarcinoma and used AI-driven de novo molecule generation plus molecular docking to propose a candidate binding compound (GEN_42). This is early-stage computational drug discovery with no experimental validation in cells or animals, making it preliminary bench science rather than a clinically actionable AI result.

scored.title: Prevalence and Risk Factors of Maternal Anemia Among Pregnant Women in Central Jordan.
scored.why: This cross-sectional survey of 297 pregnant women in Jordan used logistic regression and a multilayer perceptron neural network to identify risk factors for maternal anemia, with both models achieving roughly 71-73% accuracy, and found associations with gestational stage, abortion history, and supplement use. The neural network adds little beyond confirming standard logistic regression findings, and the small single-country survey design limits generalizability.

scored.title: Second Trimester Maternal Serum microRNAs as Biomarkers for Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia Severity.
scored.why: This study used random forest machine learning to identify three microRNAs (miRNAs) in second-trimester maternal serum that distinguish survivors from non-survivors among fetuses with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH), reporting an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.89 in a single-center cohort. The machine learning component is a minor analytic tool layered on a small, unvalidated biomarker discovery study, and the authors themselves note the need for multi-institutional validation before any clinical application.

scored.title: Frequency-specific gyro-sulcal functional differentiation in preterm neonates: Sulcal dominance and gene expression correlates.
scored.why: This study used a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) on resting-state functional MRI (fMRI) data from 437 neonates to identify frequency-specific functional differences between brain gyri and sulci across preterm and term groups, linking these patterns to cortical gene expression. The work is exploratory basic neuroscience without a defined clinical endpoint or prediction task, and its relevance to this reader's clinical AI and reproductive focus is tangential at best.

scored.title: Decoding the silent language of embryos: current evidence, clinical applicability and future perspectives of non-invasive embryo assessment in IVF.
scored.why: This is a narrative review summarizing non-invasive embryo assessment strategies in in vitro fertilization (IVF), including time-lapse monitoring, artificial intelligence-based evaluation, omics biomarkers, and non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (niPGT-A), concluding that most approaches remain investigational pending prospective multicenter validation. As a review with no original data or new findings, it offers useful context but no new evidence for this reader to act on.

scored.title: Semen analysis external quality assessment: a paradigm shift from statistical consensus to biological variation-based analytical quality specifications.
scored.why: This review synthesizes 34 years of external quality assessment (EQA) data for semen analysis, documenting large interlaboratory coefficients of variation and proposing a shift toward biological variation-based analytical quality specifications, while briefly noting that AI-assisted morphology assessment shows systematic bias relative to manual microscopy. The AI component is a minor subtopic within a broader laboratory medicine quality-control review, and no new AI validation data are presented.

scored.title: The maternal blood transcriptome reflects bovine fetal traits and can be harnessed to predict fetal sex during the first trimester.
scored.why: This study used RNA sequencing of maternal blood in cattle to identify gene expression biomarkers predicting fetal sex, validated across small bovine datasets with accuracies of 0.75 to 1.00. It is a veterinary differential expression study with no artificial intelligence component and no human reproductive application, so it falls outside the clinical AI and reproductive medicine beats despite superficial similarity.

scored.title: Current Status of Animal Models for Premature Ovarian Insufficiency: Similarities to Clinical Manifestations and Therapeutic Applications.
scored.why: This is a narrative review comparing animal models of premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) to human disease, summarizing stem cell and extracellular vesicle (EV) therapies, with artificial intelligence mentioned only as a future research direction in the final sentence. There is no original AI methodology or evaluation here, making it low priority for a clinical AI-focused reader.

scored.title: Machine learning-assisted design of a novel crocin-loaded poloxamer 407/hyaluronic acid in situ forming hydrogel for endometriosis treatment: in vitro characterization and in vivo efficacy evaluation.
scored.why: This study used an artificial neural network (ANN) to optimize the formulation parameters of a crocin-loaded hydrogel for topical endometriosis treatment, with evaluation limited to in vitro gelation properties and an in vivo rodent efficacy model. The machine learning component is a minor formulation optimization tool rather than a clinical or diagnostic application, and the biological findings are preclinical, so this is of limited relevance to clinical AI in reproductive medicine.

scored.title: The inverted pyramid of care in modern-day obstetrics.
scored.why: This Policy Forum argues for restructuring antenatal care around early risk stratification, the inverted pyramid of care concept, and briefly mentions future integration of artificial intelligence-assisted technologies without describing any specific tool or evaluation. It is a commentary piece advocating a care model rather than presenting new AI research or clinical data.

scored.title: Attitudes of pregnant women toward AI-enabled robotic nursing in obstetric and newborn care: A mixed-methods study with implications for healthcare work.
scored.why: This mixed-methods survey of 114 pregnant women in Turkey assessed attitudes toward AI-enabled robotic nursing using a validated attitude scale and semi-structured interviews, finding no significant subgroup differences except by education level. This is a perception study with no AI system evaluation or clinical outcome, so it offers limited actionable insight for a reader focused on clinical AI performance.

scored.title: Understanding Mothers' Experiences of Very Low Birth Weight Infants Across the Childbirth Trajectory in Japan: A Retrospective Analysis Using Natural Language Processing.
scored.why: This retrospective study applied natural language processing (NLP) and structural topic modeling to Japanese parent-support class notebooks from 280 mothers of very low birth weight infants, identifying thematic shifts in maternal narratives from self-blame near birth to routine caregiving concerns later. This is a descriptive qualitative application of text analysis without any predictive or clinical decision-making component, making it of limited direct relevance to clinical AI practice.

scored.title: A systematic approach to standardizing the visual appearance of endometriotic lesions for artificial intelligence recognition.
scored.why: This is a systematic literature review that synthesizes published descriptions of laparoscopic endometriosis lesion appearance into a visual ontology intended to standardize future annotation for artificial intelligence (AI) training, but no AI model is built or tested here. As a groundwork document it may be useful downstream, but it contains no actual algorithm performance data for this reader's beats.

scored.title: Habitat heterogeneity analysis of planning CT improves the prediction of radiation proctitis in cervical cancer: A multimodal machine learning study.
scored.why: A small retrospective single-institution study (n=100, with an independent test set of only 30) built a multimodal machine learning model incorporating CT-derived habitat heterogeneity radiomics to predict radiation proctitis after cervical cancer radiotherapy, reporting training AUC of 0.929 and test AUC of 0.869. The tiny sample size and lack of external multi-center validation limit confidence in generalizability despite the promising numbers.

scored.title: Clinical applications of digital twin technology in In Vitro Fertilisation.
scored.why: This is a narrative review (not a systematic review) summarizing proposed concepts of digital twin technology for in vitro fertilization (IVF), covering embryo selection, ovarian stimulation, and endometrial receptivity modeling without presenting original data or validated outcomes. The authors themselves note that large-scale randomized controlled trials (RCTs) remain absent, so this is speculative synthesis rather than evidence of impact.

scored.title: Automated precise recognition of ovine embryo microscopic images using a boundary-enhanced deep learning network.
scored.why: This study developed a boundary-enhanced deep learning network (BE-DFNet) for instance segmentation of sheep embryo microscopy images across early cleavage stages, outperforming the general-purpose Cellpose-SAM model on panoptic quality and endpoint error metrics. The work is purely a technical imaging advance in veterinary animal reproduction with no direct application to human assisted reproduction demonstrated here.

scored.title: Clinical artificial intelligence competence in obstetrics and gynecology: patient safety, physician accountability, and responsible use.
scored.why: This is a clinical opinion article proposing a framework of clinical artificial intelligence (AI) competence for obstetrician-gynecologists, discussing risks like hallucinated outputs and deskilling without presenting new data, trials, or deployment evidence. It is thoughtful commentary but falls under reviews and opinion pieces that the digest generally deprioritizes absent a field-defining claim.

scored.title: A multi-dimensional computational screening strategy for rapid identification of active components from traditional chinese medicine: Validation and application in Liangdi decoction against endometriosis.
scored.why: This study used molecular docking, multi-criteria decision analysis, and machine learning to screen bioactive components of a traditional Chinese medicine decoction for activity against endometriosis-related receptors, validated with molecular dynamics and surface plasmon resonance experiments. This is preclinical drug discovery informatics rather than clinical artificial intelligence (AI) applied to patient care, placing it at the margins of the reproductive health beat with no clinical data presented.

scored.title: Use of chat GPT for sentiment and readability analysis of nutrition articles in legacy media.
scored.why: This study used ChatGPT to perform sentiment and readability analysis of nutrition articles in legacy media, finding the AI's assessments matched a human coder and that higher reading-level articles had more positive sentiment. This is an application of a large language model (LLM) as a text-analysis tool for media content, not patient communication or clinical care, so it falls outside the intended scope of this beat.

scored.title: A Conversational Agent for Providing Personalized Preexposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) Support: Protocol for Chatbot Implementation and Evaluation.
scored.why: This is a protocol paper describing the planned iterative development and evaluation design of a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) chatbot intended to provide personalized preexposure prophylaxis (PrEP) support, with no results yet reported beyond describing the development process. As a protocol without outcome data, it cannot be judged on clinical impact and is conservatively scored low pending the actual evaluation.

scored.title: Toward a Framework for Assessing Patient-Facing Gen AI Tools in Mental Healthcare.
scored.why: This is a systematic review synthesizing 72 studies to propose a four-domain framework for pre-deployment assessment of generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) mental health tools, with no new empirical data or clinical evaluation of a specific system. As commentary and framework-building rather than a result that changes practice, it scores low under the review-exclusion criterion for this beat.

scored.title: Accuracy and limitations of artificial intelligence chatbots in answering patient questions on scoliosis surgery.
scored.why: This study had two orthopedic surgeons rate responses from three AI chatbots to 25 frequently asked questions about scoliosis surgery using a 4-point accuracy and clarity scale, finding ChatGPT-4o performed best. This is a small rubric-based comparison among chatbots without a clinician-generated comparator or any measured patient impact, making it routine for this beat.

scored.title: Navigating AI in Mental Health Care and Psychotherapy: Proposing the GUIDE Framework.
scored.why: This is a conceptual, unvalidated framework (GUIDE) proposing how clinicians should discuss patient use of large language models (LLMs) in psychotherapy, with no empirical evaluation of outcomes or comparison to clinician practice. It offers opinion and structure rather than data, so it is low-yield for a reader tracking measured effects of AI on patient care.

scored.title: Reliability, quality, and readability levels of ChatGPT-5.2 responses regarding office ergonomics: Analysis of content based on Google Trends.
scored.why: This is a single-day, single-model, keyword-based rubric evaluation of ChatGPT-5.2's office ergonomics answers, scored on quality, reliability, and readability indices with good inter-rater agreement via intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). It offers no clinician-answer comparator, workload measure, or patient outcome, making it a routine readability audit rather than a finding that should change practice.

scored.title: Conversational Agents for Asthma and Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Management: Scoping Review.
scored.why: This scoping review of 15 studies on conversational agents (CAs) for asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) finds that only 4 studies measured direct clinical outcomes, with most evidence being small feasibility or pilot work. As a review with no new data or clinician comparison, it is useful context but not itself a finding that should reorient the reader's work.

scored.title: When Treatment Gets More Complicated: AI Readability Declines in Breast Cancer Patient Education.
scored.why: This study used automated linguistic and readability metrics (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, SMOG, Gunning Fog) plus LIWC-22 psycholinguistic software to compare ChatGPT and Gemini outputs on breast cancer patient education, finding both exceed recommended reading levels and that finer psycholinguistic differences did not survive false discovery rate (FDR) correction. This is a routine readability and style comparison with no clinician benchmark or patient outcome, so it adds little beyond confirming known readability gaps.

scored.title: Applications of generative artificial intelligence in chronic pain: a scoping review.
scored.why: This scoping review of 25 studies on generative artificial intelligence (AI) in chronic pain finds most evidence is based on model performance or expert ratings rather than prospective clinical outcomes, with persistent issues of hallucination and limited external validation. As a review summarizing known limitations without new data, it offers little beyond confirming the field's early stage.

scored.title: Evaluating the Reliability, Accuracy, and Readability of ChatGPT-3.5 and GPT-4 in Providing Patient Education Related to Glenohumeral Joint Osteoarthritis.
scored.why: Four fellowship-trained shoulder surgeons rated ChatGPT-3.5 and GPT-4 responses to glenohumeral osteoarthritis questions on a 1-5 scale across relevance, accuracy, clarity, completeness, and evidence support, with no statistically significant differences in content themes. This is another single-condition chatbot rubric evaluation without clinician-response comparison or patient outcome, making it routine for this beat.

scored.title: Assessing the performance of AI chatbots in answering common questions about Patellofemoral Pain Syndrome.
scored.why: Four AI chatbots (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity) were compared on accuracy, clarity, completeness, and readability for patellofemoral pain syndrome questions using Likert ratings and standard readability indices, finding universal failure to meet sixth-grade readability benchmarks. This is another routine multi-chatbot readability comparison without clinician benchmarking or patient-facing deployment.

scored.title: Large language models as sources of patient information on robotic knee arthroplasty: a comparative evaluation.
scored.why: Three orthopedic specialists rated responses from ChatGPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-Flash, and DeepSeek-V3 on robotic knee arthroplasty patient questions, finding Gemini scored highest on reliability and usefulness while being less readable, an inverse pattern between reliability and readability. This is a routine multi-model comparison using expert rubric scores with no clinician-response comparator or patient outcome data.

scored.title: Comparative Evaluation of AI Chatbots for Testicular Cancer Education: Validity, Information Quality, and Readability.
scored.why: Four chatbots were tested on 250 multiple-choice clinical knowledge questions and 12 patient-facing questions about testicular cancer, with ChatGPT 5.2 scoring highest on both structured accuracy (98.4%) and information quality scales like DISCERN and Global Quality Scale (GQS), but all models failed sixth-grade readability benchmarks. This is another routine chatbot benchmarking study without clinician comparison or real-world deployment, offering incremental confirmation of known readability gaps.

scored.title: The Role and Impact of Artificial Intelligence in Preventive Dentistry: A Scoping Review.
scored.why: This scoping review of 43 studies covers AI applications in preventive dentistry, including risk prediction, self-monitoring, and patient education chatbots, finding AI tools generally match human experts in risk stratification but with limited standardization. As a broad review spanning multiple non-communication AI applications with only a small chatbot subset, it offers minimal depth on the LLM-patient beat specifically.

scored.title: Challenges of AI-generated stigmatizing language regarding substance use disorders.
scored.why: This is an opinion and discussion piece arguing that large language models (LLMs) may reproduce stigmatizing language about substance use disorders found in their training data, including electronic health records, and calling for clinician involvement in refining model outputs. No original data, evaluation, or deployment is presented, making it commentary rather than evidence.

scored.title: Who Trusts AI for Health Information? A Cross-National Survey on Trust Determinants in Four European Countries.
scored.why: A cross-national survey using structural equation modeling examined psychological and social predictors of trust in AI-generated health information across four European countries, finding AI literacy and performance expectancy as consistent predictors. This is a social-science survey with no clinical evaluation, patient outcome, or comparison to clinicians, so it falls outside the kind of evidence this beat values.

scored.title: Generative AI at the Bedside: An Integrative Review of Applications and Implications in Clinical Nursing Practice.
scored.why: This is an integrative review synthesizing existing literature on generative AI use in nursing practice, covering workflow, clinical reasoning, patient communication, and ethics themes, without presenting new primary data. As a review of secondary sources, it offers context but no new evaluation or evidence relevant to judging LLM performance against clinicians.

scored.title: Comment on "Customized Education Sheets Generated by ChatGPT Improve Parental Visit Satisfaction and Procedural Knowledge Prior to Pediatric Cardiac Catheterization".
scored.why: This is a letter commenting on a prior single-center quality improvement study of ChatGPT-generated education sheets for pediatric cardiac catheterization, raising methodological critiques such as the lack of a control group and inappropriate use of parametric statistics on ordinal data. As commentary rather than original research, it adds no new evidence despite being a reasonable critique.

scored.title: The Usability and Experience of Artificial Intelligence-Based Conversational Agents in Health Education for Cancer Patients: A Scoping Review.
scored.why: This scoping review synthesizes 12 studies on the usability and patient experience of AI-based conversational agents in cancer health education, identifying themes like insufficient customization and lack of empathy, but presents no new primary data. As a review of existing literature without original evaluation, it offers limited new evidence for this beat.

scored.title: MedCity FemFwd: Opportunities in the Fertility Market
scored.why: This is a podcast episode discussing a PwC advisory report on opportunities in the fertility and reproductive health market, with no specific product, funding figure, or regulatory action described. As a discussion of a third-party market report rather than concrete company or regulatory action, it falls short of the threshold for industry news this beat values.

scored.title: Licensure Framework for Autonomous Clinical Artificial Intelligence.
scored.why: This is a letter responding to a prior JAMA Viewpoint on licensure frameworks for autonomous clinical artificial intelligence (AI), with no abstract or original data provided. Correspondence of this kind contributes to policy discussion but contains no new evidence for this reader's purposes.

scored.title: Licensure Framework for Autonomous Clinical Artificial Intelligence.
scored.why: Another letter in the same correspondence thread on licensure frameworks for autonomous clinical artificial intelligence (AI), with no text or data supplied. Not substantive research for this digest.

scored.title: Licensure Framework for Autonomous Clinical Artificial Intelligence.
scored.why: A third letter in the licensure framework correspondence series, again with no abstract or data. Purely discursive, not research.

scored.title: Licensure Framework for Autonomous Clinical Artificial Intelligence-In Reply.
scored.why: The original authors' reply within the same correspondence thread on licensure frameworks for autonomous clinical artificial intelligence (AI); no text provided. Not a research contribution.

scored.title: Licensure Framework for Autonomous Clinical Artificial Intelligence.
scored.why: A fourth letter in the same correspondence series on licensure frameworks for autonomous clinical artificial intelligence (AI), with no abstract available. Not substantive for this reader's research interests.

scored.title: What Parents Need to Know About AI as a New Kind of Listener.
scored.why: No abstract text was provided for this JAMA Pediatrics piece on AI as a listener for parents, and the title suggests a general-audience advisory piece rather than original research. Without substantive content, it cannot be scored as meaningful clinical AI evidence.

scored.title: MRI Characteristics of Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease: A Review.
scored.why: This is a clinical review of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features in myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD), with artificial intelligence (AI) mentioned only briefly as a future direction rather than evaluated. It contains no AI methodology, evaluation, or outcome data, placing it outside the scope of the clinical AI beats despite its clinical value for neuroradiology.

scored.title: Organoids: Current Applications and Future Directions.
scored.why: This is a broad narrative review of organoid technology across multiple organ systems, mentioning artificial intelligence only as one of several emerging tools alongside CRISPR, multiomics, and organ-on-chip platforms. It contains no original research, no clinical AI application, and minimal reproductive-specific content beyond a brief mention of endometrial organoids.

scored.title: Ending maternal deaths in Africa: An agenda for the African Academy of Sciences.
scored.why: This is an opinion and advocacy piece calling on the African Academy of Sciences to address maternal mortality, mentioning artificial intelligence only in passing as part of a broader vision for technological progress. It contains no study design, data, or AI methodology and is not a research contribution.

scored.title: A Comprehensive Review of Strategies to Enhance Quality and Safety in Infertility Laboratories.
scored.why: This narrative review discusses quality and safety strategies in assisted reproductive technology (ART) laboratories, including witnessing systems and quality management, with artificial intelligence tools mentioned only briefly as an emerging safeguard. There is no original research, evaluation, or AI methodology described, so it offers little new information for this reader.

scored.title: Research trends in artificial intelligence use in women's health (from 1992 to 2024): A bibliometric analysis.
scored.why: This is a bibliometric analysis mapping publication trends, authors, institutions, and keywords for artificial intelligence research in women's health from 1992 to 2024, using citation and co-occurrence software. It contains no original clinical finding or AI evaluation and is purely descriptive of the literature landscape, so it offers minimal actionable content for this reader.

scored.title: Spotlights on Cervical Cancer: Progression, Diagnosis and Clinical Manifestations, Epidemiology, Treatment Approaches, Role of Artificial Intelligence and Future Directions.
scored.why: This is a broad narrative review covering cervical cancer epidemiology, diagnosis, treatment, and briefly artificial intelligence applications in screening and robotic surgical planning, without presenting original data or a focused evaluation. As a general review spanning many non-AI topics like nanotechnology and immunotherapy, it offers little specific new information for a clinical AI-focused reader.

scored.title: Integrated proteomics and metabolomics for predicting cardiometabolic risk in pregnant women living with HIV: current evidence and future directions.
scored.why: This review discusses proteomic and metabolomic biomarker approaches for predicting cardiometabolic risk in pregnant women living with HIV, mentioning machine learning only as one of several analytic methods used across the broader literature. It explicitly notes that integrated proteomic-metabolomic prediction studies in this population remain scarce, making this an agenda-setting review rather than a substantive AI or clinical finding.

scored.title: Machine learning prediction of euploid pregnancy loss: validation is not prevention.
scored.why: This item's title, 'Machine learning prediction of euploid pregnancy loss: validation is not prevention,' suggests a critical commentary on machine learning risk prediction models in reproductive medicine, but no abstract or study text was provided. Without any methodological or findings detail, this cannot be meaningfully evaluated and should be scored conservatively.

scored.title: Theoretical model and parameter optimization of embryo eggshell perforation under impact.
scored.why: This study optimizes mechanical parameters for perforating chicken eggshells before in-ovo vaccination using a genetic algorithm-backpropagation (GA-BP) neural network, achieving an R-squared of 0.91 for predicting shell damage. It has no connection to human reproductive medicine or clinical AI and sits entirely within poultry industry engineering.

scored.title: Unveiling the identification of the genetic features and biological characteristics shared between cervical cancer and venous thromboembolism.
scored.why: This bioinformatics study uses protein-protein interaction networks and machine learning (Lasso, XGBoost, generalized linear model, random forest) to find shared hub genes between cervical cancer and venous thromboembolism, reporting a training AUC of 0.964 for a nomogram model. It is a gene-expression biomarker discovery study with no clinical deployment or reproductive-imaging relevance, placing it outside the scope of these beats.

scored.title: Advances in computational anthropomorphic phantoms and Monte Carlo-based dosimetry: A review.
scored.why: This is a review of computational anthropomorphic phantoms and Monte Carlo dosimetry methods used in radiation physics, covering historical developments from stylized geometries to mesh-based models including maternal and fetal phantoms. It contains no original clinical AI research and no reproductive health findings, making it off-topic for all three beats.

scored.title: A randomized controlled trial evaluating the use of an intelligent, fully automated 2-dimensional imaging system to detect lame cows and control lameness.
scored.why: This randomized controlled trial (RCT) tested an automated machine-learning-based imaging system for detecting lameness in dairy cows, showing lower rates of severe and chronic lameness in the intervention group. Despite rigorous RCT design, the subject is veterinary animal husbandry with no connection to human reproductive or clinical medicine.

scored.title: Principal component analysis-based three-dimensional quantitative characterization of cracks on perforated embryo eggs.
scored.why: This study used principal component analysis (PCA) and a random forest classifier on 3D point-cloud reconstructions to characterize eggshell cracks in poultry eggs used for vaccine virus cultivation, reporting 99.19% mean accuracy in crack shape classification. It concerns industrial egg quality control for vaccine manufacturing, not human reproductive or clinical medicine, and is off-topic for this digest.

scored.title: Sleep Disorders and Male Infertility: Integrated Mechanisms and Precision Therapeutic Strategies.
scored.why: This is a narrative review synthesizing mechanistic links between sleep disorders and male infertility, proposing a conceptual framework involving oxidative stress, circadian disruption, and epigenetics, with no new data, algorithm, or AI component. It is off-topic for the AI-focused beats and belongs more to basic andrology commentary than to clinical AI or reproductive AI research.

scored.title: Comment on "Readability and performance of AI chatbot responses to frequently asked questions in maxillofacial prosthodontics".
scored.why: This is a letter/comment with no abstract or substantive content provided, responding to a prior study on chatbot readability in maxillofacial prosthodontics. There is nothing here to evaluate for clinical or research significance.

scored.title: Response to the Letter to the Editor, "Comment on 'Readability and performance of AI chatbot responses to frequently asked questions in maxillofacial prosthodontics'".
scored.why: This is an author response to a letter to the editor, with no abstract or substantive content provided. There is no new data or finding to assess.

scored.title: Corrigendum to "Integration of Inflammatory and Nutritional Biomarkers with Machine Learning Enhances Prediction of Progesterone Response in Fertility-Preserving Endometrial Carcinoma Management" [Translational Oncology volume 71 (2026) 102897].
scored.why: This is a corrigendum, a correction notice, for a previously published article on machine learning prediction of progesterone response in endometrial carcinoma, with no abstract or substantive content provided. There is nothing here for this reader to act on.

scored.title: Byakangelicin alleviates metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis by selective inhibition of a non-canonical MTORC1 signaling pathway.
scored.why: This is a basic science mechanistic study on a natural compound's effect on a signaling pathway in metabolic liver disease in mice, with no artificial intelligence component and no connection to reproductive or women's health. It falls entirely outside the scope of all three beats covered by this digest.
